text: We had a lovely birthday lunch for my wife at the Fountain Restaurant. From the moment we entered, the host, server, and even the person who brought the water to the table wished my wife a happy birthday. Our server, Antionette, was very professional yet friendly, and offered some excellent advice as to what to choose for the entrees. We started off with some pulled pork sliders and some asian chicken dumplings. Both were fine but nothing special and I was starting to worry that we were in for just an average meal. However, once our entrees arrived, the food became spectacular. My wife had fabulous, perfectly prepared scallops, and on Antoinette's recommendation, my son had a delicious salmon club sandwich. I had the moroccan salmon that was sushi grade so I ordered it rare. It had to be by far the best salmon I have ever tasted in my life (and I probably have had a lot of salmon). It was not overly spicy and was served over two different sauces with chickpeas and yellow raisins. After our entrees were served, Antoinette brought out a birthday treat for my wife (pictured) that we all shared. It was delicious. We also tried the flourless chocolate cake and the homemade caramel, prezel, and chocolate chip ice cream, both of which were pretty good. All in all, we had a relaxing meal with excellent service. While our appetizers and two thirds of the desserts were pretty good, the entrees more than made up for it.

text: Hands down the best meal I've eaten in Nashville. I know, I know I get excited about new restaurant adventures but seriously people, if you haven't made the attempt to dine in at F. Scott's then you are missing out big time. A romantic dinner during the 2011 January restaurant week brought me and hubs-to-be out to F. Scott's for a fancy meal. All for $30.11 per person; a once or twice a year occasion. We had made reservations but at 6:30p.m. on a Wednesday evening, they weren't exactly needed. The place didn't begin to pick up until at least 7:15-7:30p.m. When we arrived into the parking lot I noticed a sign that said "Valet for Free" for F. Scott's customers. FANCY! We decided to park ourselves and as soon as we walked in we were not only greeted by the hostess but also the folks in front of us checking in for dinner. Friendly people are always a good sign. Fortunately at the moment we walked in our server, Peter, was standing at the hostess station and asked to check our coats before he brought us to our dimly lit table. FANCY and ROMANTIC! Peter was on par through out the whole meal. I ordered the salad as my first course which was a beautiful blend of romaine with roasted mushrooms, walnut and rosemary bread crumbs (adding extra supportive texture), and tossed in a Sherry Crème Fraîche vinaigrette. Simply wonderful! The onion soup (soup of the day) was hearty as well. For the main course we went for the meat and potatoes! A perfectly grilled sirloin was marinated in this sweet yet robust tomato-coffee sauce and decadently placed on a bed of mashed potatoes and garnished with crispy collard greens. A bite of everything together takes you back to your mother's kitchen with a fancy twist. Finally to end this wonderful meal was dessert. The vanilla bean crème brulée and fresh coconut cake with a chocolate sauce were divine. The entire meal was phenomenal and honestly words cannot describe my pleasure this evening during my meal. You only have to experience it for yourself.

text: I guess the food is pretty important to to the Isla Vista lifestyle. It's great drunk food, being heavy and high in saturated fat. Yes, it's tasty. Yes, you can get whatever you want, and secret menu items like the tostada can save you some money on your next visit here. but no matter what anyone says about this place, Freebirds is about the ambiance. On a given Thursday, Friday or Saturday from11:00 PM to 4:00 AM, you are going to find one of the most trashed and unpredictable groups of people you will meet in your lifetime. Whether it be in line, sitting out on the benches outside. Within your Isla Vista tenure, you will have seen and/or experienced at least three (3) of the following situations: 1)The Hot Mess: A person who's blacked out, stumbling, and in general incoherent somehow ordering their preference in nachos, either in sloppy English or PERFECT Spanish in automatic mode. Afterwards, they decide it's time to stagger home, but then they trip on the steps at Freebirds and drop all of their food and start crying. 2)COME AT ME BRO!: It's extremely rare, but sometimes two people (usually an out-of-owner and a local) get really drunk and decide that they want to take out their sexual frustration on other people. Usually it's just posturing, but when it does happen, it redefines dinner and a show. It's like Medieval times, except you can replace dudes in silly clothes jousting with dudes cavemen in silly clothes penis jousting. There's a lot of swinging, very few punches are landed, and usually someone just trips. We don't usually get into fights in Isla Vista and when we see one, we usually do our best to stop it or de-escalate a situation. I've seen people offer to share their nachos with guys that get into fights just to get them to chill the fuck out. It's a beautiful sight. 3)IV Celebrity: The Pirate or Carms or Jimmy J rolls up to freebirds and the entire place erupts in excitement. but really they're just going there to either mooch a drink off of you, steal your shit, or make you buy something, in that respective order for those people. 4)WHO ARE YOU?: You and your friends are sitting down, eating freebirds, and talking about whatever has transpired this evening. And then someone who none of you know, someone you don't particularly like, or someone who you "knew" for a night and don't want to know comes over, makes small talk, and shares nachos with you. You guys loudly whisper to yourselves "WHO THE FUCK IS THIS PERSON?" But really, at this point of the night, you're too tired to fight them off of your food and you come to accept them taking up space on your table. And one of your friends hooks up with her. 5)The Nacho Date: Two people who just met that evening either in downtown Santa Barbara, or at some party in IV, and they've hit it off. They were making out most of the way on their trip to Freebirds. At some point, they'll walk in and get nachos, and share them. It's kind of cute, really. But then this situation goes one of two ways. A) I'm too drunk to go home with you, let me sober up - Guy is too drunk to function but is going to try to take a girl home that night. He decides that he's going to have some freebirds to help him get his shit together. B) - I was blacked out: after a young lady has eaten enough, somehow she comes to. It turns out the guy who she's with is some extremely ugly Bro that's missing a front tooth, has a tattoo of his area code on his neck. She suddenly has this look of shock in her face after making eye contact with him again, and then she quietly excuses herself to the bathroom, never to return again. So really, Freebirds is about watching people and bonding over these moments with your friends as you all eat from the same styrofoam container of nachos. If anyone tells you it's about the food, they clearly have not been to Freebirds within the acceptable hours.
label: POS

text: Franny's - Home of the Throwed Rag You'll really just have to go to this place yourself to believe what I'm going to say. Harry put it perfectly when he said this place would provide all the fodder you'd ever need for a N'awlins cartoon strip. The decor is cheap circa 1970s, with panel-sided video poker cubbies added in. The scent alone is enough to knock you flat when you walk in; a combination of ancient food and bleach. Susan wanted to sit in a booth, and every vinyl bench she approached was wet from a recent wipe-down. A waitress yelled from across the room - "Just sit anywhere!!!!". When we said we couldn't sit on a wet booth seat - "They dry in a few minutes, just sit down!". Of course! Please understand, the place was almost empty. A dry rag couldn't make its way to the seats? No it couldn't, because they were closing in a half hour. Garnet, our waitress, was priceless. Somehow in the course of exchanging under 250 words, she actually said a sentence that contained the words "fried pig s***". Wow! Did I actually hear that?? Oh, I was ready for a hearty breakfast after that! Now, I will have to say that the coffee was decent. Don't go looking for decaf, though, because it's instant. We ordered a big breakfast, a pork chop breakfast, an order of eggs and hash browns, and the pecan waffle. Everyone's eggs were very runny, and the yolks were lemon-yellow. The color and water content of the yolk was indicative of a more cheaply produced egg, one where they definitely are not feeding the chickens extra Omega-3s for a healthy diet. While no pecans had ever seen the battter that constituted my "pecan" waffle, it was tasty! Had a somewhat nutty, whole-wheat flavor. It was cooked a bit too long, but it was by far the best thing anyone had on the table. The most hilarious moment came when Garnet delivered the syrup to our table. It was Value Time syrup. It surely must have been procured from Dollar Tree. It was a 48 oz. bottle of watery HF corn syrup. Hey, I asked for syrup, I didn't say what type! Susan suggested I ask again, but for maple syrup. I wonder what response that might have brought? Harry's bacon looked like it had been cooking under a flat iron for two hours. It was the flattest, driest bacon ever. But, in fairness, the guys ate every scrap of their breakfast meats, so I guess they're doing something right here. Garnet busied herself by taking every piece of dishware she could get from us as quickly as possible, since they were closing in 20 minutes. We all know the difference between good service or "get out of here" mode from a server. We were getting the treatment, that's for sure! The climactic moment came when a rag, doubtlessly the same rag that was used to wipe down our moist bench seats before we arrived, was catapulted practically across our table. The waitresses, Garnet and accomplice, could not waste a moment to exchange the rag between hands, otherwise how would they leave the building in five minutes? So, the rag flew past us at eye level to cover 4 yards before reaching its destination. Touchdown! Speaking of touchdowns, the entire decor, and playlist, of Franny's is New Orleans Saints-themed. We did enjoy singing "Who Let the Dogs Out" before we departed. Where was Nat'ly this morning? Where was Vic? They must have been there earlier.
label: NEG

After an entire group was served, the bartender would then ring up the drinks. Then run the card. Each step seems minor, but adds to an unnecessary wait. There should be multiple people at each register to streamline this process as there is usually 20 minutes between shows and 25 minutes spent in line? One person should make the drinks, while another swipes the cards all at the same time. Many people were ordering mixed drinks, which is fine, but for those who just want a quick over-priced brew in a can, we should not have to wait in 30 people lines for such. text: The Grand Sierra hotel (don't kid yourself, this is not a "resort") feels like the kind of place that might go out of business while you're staying there. This past weekend my wife and I booked a two night stay at the Grand Sierra and after the first night we checked out and switched hotels, it's that bad. The lobby and casino are nice enough. After the burn-out stoner snowboarder parks your car and you get inside you might even be tricked into thinking this is a nice place. Not so. I read another review on line that described the hallways in this hotel as something out of the Shining, and that's a dead-on accurate description. Murky, dark, loooooong corridors with a bizarre mixture of pseudo-Native American/Southwest inspired designs and an off-putting green/burnt orange color scheme come together to make you certain that around the next corner (if you ever get there) you'll find a pile of hacked up children. If the goal is to get you to RUN to your room and RUN to the casino... goal achieved, I don't want to spend any more time in this creepy hallway than I have to. As for the rooms themselves... well... 1989 called and wants their TV's back. I haven't seen a TV this old outside of a pawn shop. Uncomfortable beds? Check. Cramped old fashioned bathroom with hideous wall paper? Check. Backwards rotating knobs in the shower so you get sprayed with freezing water? Check. Low shower nozzle that bashes you in the head while trying to shampoo? Check. Horrible view of a parking lot out the window? Check. Sign threatening to charge you for the bathrobe and coffee maker that *weren't even in the room in the first place*? Check. OK, well what about the other parts of the "resort". First let's brave the creepy Stephen King elevators that open their yawning mouths as if they'll swallow you up forever. Beneath the casino is the arcade level. Down in the bowels of the hotel the hallways are easily 20 feet wide, you could race Hummers side-by-side down here, and it's just as murky and creepy as the hallways to the rooms. Honestly it feels like something out of a post-apolcalyptic zombie flick, this is where people would hole up to try and survive while sending out the strongest to hunt for food and fire wood. The few "shops" downstairs all have the odor of imminent death as well, not a single soul inside doing any shopping. The actual arcade is nice, plenty of games and a big play area for the kids, plus one star. But the other businesses on this level feel like any minute you might see a crying owner shuttering the doors and then you'd hear a gunshot and a thud as their lifeless body crumples to the ground. Seriously. This place is awful. I've never been in a hotel before where I could almost literally hear the wind sighing the words "Geeeeeeeet oooouuuuuuttttttt". Let's check out the pool, it should be nice. Ooops, CLOSED. Let me wend my way past the area where pets are brought outside to poop and then, yep, past the smoking section.... wow this place really could use some landscaping... and paint.... and art.... and a wrecking ball..... Back upstairs, we checked out the bowling alley. Very nice! Well lit, lots of people, clean... it served as a stark counterpoint to the dank, weird chasm we had just emerged from downstairs. Anyways you get the point. This place bites. And if that's not all enough here's a couple of other jtems: - 20 minute wait on hold on the phone to get the front desk to initiate our early checkout, when I mentioned the hold time I was told "Yeah, that's cuz we're busy." - Pool = Closed. No indoor pool - Spa = No towel racks? No bench to set things one? Ok I'll just put my stuff... on the... floor? Thanks. We normally stay at the Atlantis, and thought we'd try something "different". Ooooops. We went to the Atlantis for the next night, it was great. Steer clear of the Grand Sierra unless you're one of the producers of Ghost Hunters or some other show that highlights old places full of spooky, lonely hallways and not much else of any interest. One star, plus one star for nice arcade, bowling alley and casino. Visit if you want, but DO NOT stay here.

text: I haven't been this excited to write a review for a while! Zahav's restaurant menu looked very appetizing (soon learned they have the same menu regularly @ $39/pp) to pass up. I could've done without the rice pilaf. - The beef & lamb meatballs (kofte) was delicous, cumin is my new favorite spice. - For dessert, the ricotta filled phyllo dough topped with ice cream was warm and tasty! I don't know how they got the dough like that, but I can eat that everyday. Loved the decor of low ambient lighting and open face kitchen that you can look into. It's not a really large place and that's probably why reservations were so limited. Zahav will be on my list to frequent more and I'll recommend it to everyone! The next few days and nothing satisfied my palette! :( I can't wait to go back. Hard to believe that it's associated with Percy Street BBQ because I did not get the same experience there. text: A dear friend of mine has raved about Neo of Melaka for quite awhile so I decided it was time to give it a try. Service started off a bit spotty. So we waited in the middle of the restaurant, a bit unsure of what to do. Were we to seat ourselves? We picked a booth and let the fella know. We started off with iced Malaysian tea and an iced coffee. Loved our drinks!! Great flavor and perfect sweetness. Next- the spring rolls were a tasty appetizer. I truly wish I would have conferred with dear friend mentioned previously in my review because I had a difficult time deciding what to have for dinner. Eventually decided on a noodle and tofu lemongrass dish. It didn't mention that it was spicy but spicy is indeed what it was! Absolutely had a great flavor to it. Highly enjoyed my meal and it was such a generous portion that I have left-overs. My dining partner had a meal that was not what she had anticipated but our server was happy to replace it with another choice. You may want to ask about ingredients in Neo's meals if you have any dietary restrictions, as that was the reason that she needed to have a change made. My favorite part of the meal was dessert! Amanda A recommended that we try the red bean ice cream. Oh my yummy! I want more! So my big suggestion would be to save room for dessert at Neo.

text: There are many good things to say about Rambla, but these are somewhat incidental. In just one dining experience, it became quite clear to me that this restaurant does not take itself seriously. Any restaurant can have a bad night, but it takes persistent inattention to punctuate an entire meal with oversights. Problems included both the front of the house and the kitchen. The menu and wine list were missing several items that we ordered. In the case of the wine, the first two bottles were unavailable, but the server was not able to warn us without going on a trek to determine availability. Finally, I just agreed to a recommendation to avoid further disruption of the meal, but it was distinctly sub par. On the fourth try, we were able to get a great wine at a reasonable price. The hole in the menu was addressed in an equally ham handed way. We ordered only to have the waiter return later to tell us that something was unavailable. If there are enough items unavailable that the server can't warn diners before they order, it is time to change the menu. The level of service attention was not what I would describe as a meltdown, but it was problematic. Since we were the only table, I would hate to see what might ensue as things get busy. Although the lamb cheeks were a bit dry, most dishes displayed technical precision. In some cases the portions were peculiar both with respect to the content of the dish and the menu price. Overall, Rambla is a mixed bag with prices that should accompany something much closer to perfection.
label: NEG

text: The only thing worse than bad food is good food that's been ruined. Tonight, I ordered a fried chicken wing platter. For $10, it came with two sides and cornbread. Not great, but not bad. I chose potato salad and seafood/pasta salad. I specifically made a note and asked for the wings to be "fried hard," aka well done. About 45 minutes later, the delivery guy called my phone, as I requested, to announce his arrival. You would think that in the time it took me to get downstairs and answer the door, he would have made his way to my door, but no. I answered the door in my pajamas, and had to stand there and wait as he very slowly walked up to my door. I mean exaggeratedly slow as though he were testing me to see if I would come to him and save him the trouble. Absolutely not. I gave you a $5 tip. Bring me my sh*t and quickly, so I'm not standing there being ogled by my nosey neighbors, letting the bugs in and letting the air conditioning out. I absolutely would have stiffed him on the tip had I not already pre-paid it through Grub Hub. I've gotta stop doing that. When I saw the way the food was packed, my heart sunk. Why, if you specialize in fried foods - they sell chicken wings and fish and whatever else - do you not know how to package them so that they arrive in the best condition? These places have no pride in their product. Or they don't have enough sense to test the food and see what it looks and tastes like after 30mins to a hour packed in unventilated styrofoam and airtight plastic? The bag was tied shut. I was devastated. I knew my chicken wings would be soggy. I prayed the styrofoam container had at least been vented and POSSIBLY the steam had gone elsewhere and not condensed on my crispy wings. As I struggled to open the knotted and sealed bag, I knew it would be bad. I was sure the bag had sucked the life out of my food, and my sole consolation was hoping the tiny holes in the corners of the containers had been punched out. Of course, they weren't, and, I screamed. DAMN, DAMN, DAMN! The styrofoam containers have punch-out vents for a reason. USE THEM! Steam is not cute on (supposed to be) crispy food. Then I opened the container, and MOTHER OF GOD... the cold salads and hot chicken were all in the same container. HOW DISRESPECTFUL!! Sure enough, the wings were wet and sitting in a puddle of grease and water from the steam being trapped and returning to water as it cooled. As I fought my gag reflex - mushy crust is the stuff nightmares are made of - and bit into the chicken, I was at once happy and devastated even further. The seasoning was delicious. It is hard to come by a really well-seasoned chicken wing, but this was a pretty good job. But the freaking things were not well done. They were cooked through, but just barely, and, therefore, hard to pull apart, even though I specifically asked that they be fried hard. I put the chicken down and tried the potato salad. It was delicious, almost as good as my momma's, but the top layer of the potato salad was hot. That is just GROSS. I can't even explain how bad it is. I am a potato-salad freak and this... omg. You know on the TV shows where the snobby critic refuses to eat the food for some seemingly inane reason... That is how I felt. I tried the pasta salad. Also delicious, even though it was hot on top. This is not such a tragedy, though, as the hot potato salad. The shrimp in it were either entirely overdone in preparation, or they were made that way by the steam forced to live in the container. The cornbread wasn't bad, but it was tough like they beat the batter too much, and kind of bland. I guess it's what cornbread is supposed to be. Good food ruined. Next time, I will pick up the food myself and package it properly for transport. I'm sure, if they fry my wings long enough, they'll get at least 3 stars next time around.

There was a mushy pulled pork sandwich at my table, that I had no interest in trying having seen it. The Bacon Sampler, pretty darn tasty. Overpriced, but novel and tasty. I was rather impressed by the fresh oysters. But the drinks, major fail. The whole reason for coming was the promise of a good cocktail or three. I got one. A solidly made standard, a Negroni. Well, I'm certainly not ordering another one of those, and I ask to have the barman make his "best" drink. This is a cocktail bar; a "Bartender's Battle", cut glass barware, small batch bitters kind of cocktail bar. And I have just given the barman carte blanch to create and serve anything he likes, I'll pay for it. You know what I get?, a Dark & Stormy. Rum and soda, ginger flavored soda mind you, in a glass. 'Nuff said, Fail. Do not pass Go, Do not Collect $200. The bill was more like $300, but you get the point. Thanks Indy.

text: My wife and I were excited to hear of the opening of Bailey's Range. The description on-line led us to believe it was similar to a great place we used to visit back in Alabama called Baja Burger. Very unique burgers with amazing flavor combinations. Bailey's seemed to promise a similar experience. Our visit, however, left a bit to be desired. But, before I give the negatives, let me offer a few positives. First off, the decor and design of the restaurant are very interesting and fresh. Since we decided to sit at the bar, we were taken care of by the bartender, who was very friendly and attentive. Big plus on that one. Finally, the beer selection was possibly the best I have seen around. Almost every local craft brewery was on tap, including the fairly newcomer Perennial Artisan Ales. And, not just their flagship offerings, but multiple choices from each brewer. Major bonus for a hop head like me! Ok, now for the review of the food. My wife ordered the Blackened Blue beef burger and I chose the Thai Chicken Burger. We also ordered some pretzels and cheese sauce. Their descriptions of the burgers sounded very appealing, so we were both excited. That is where the excitement ended. We both took our first bites and responded with "that is interesting...and different." We were both trying to give it a fair shake. So, I finished mine, mixing in the pretzels to take away from the flavor, and basically just trying to finish it. My wife ate half of hers and then was finished. Then we both took a bite of each others just to see what the other one had chosen, and still had the same response. We finished up, paid the bill and promptly left. Once we got in the car to head back home, we were recounting the meal, as we commonly do, and both had the same review...not so good. The Blackened burger had a weird flavor that was something akin to one of the ingredients being spoiled or soured. The Thai chicken burger had a very similar flavor that just seemed off. Neither one was savory or had a flavor combo that made us say "WOW". Hopefully since this is still within the first month of them opening, Bailey's Range can get things focused and can really hone in on those flavors that will make your mouth sing. Right now, for us, we won't be returning anytime soon...unless it is just for drinks and to hang at the bar.

text: Words can't describe how excited I am to have such an adequate Korean grocery store this close to me. This grocery store is mostly Korean, with some Japanese, and a sprinkling of Chinese/Vietnamese/SE Asian products. I come here every couple of weeks to stock up on supplies. They have a small case of produce that is good for picking up some hard-to-find ingredients for asian cooking, mostly Korean though. I do get my Thai basil here, so it's nice that I don't have to run up to South Philly for that. They even have chameh! The prices are reasonable, and they have a pretty good selection for the size of the store. The only thing is that the produce is more expensive than what I'm used to, but not by a lot. I could probably get it cheaper at a chain store like H-Mart, but convenience wins out. The grocery store is connected to a "gift shop" where you can find Korean home goods. They sell banchan in the back, but I haven't tried it. I've been tempted to pick some up a couple times, but I always end up changing my mind. They either don't look that fresh, or it's more than I'm willing to spend, so I usually end up making it at home. You can buy presliced meat in the freezer section. I've gotten the samgyopsal, and it's so-so. Too thin and not very porky tasting. I'd probably go out to H-Mart and shell out for the better quality stuff. I tried the jarred kimchi once, and I can't recommend it. It was pretty watery and bland. A couple times, when I've gone on Saturday, there will be dukbokki for sale next to the register, and I always pick some up if it's still warm. The texture of the rice cakes isn't as good as freshly made, but the sauce has a nice flavor.

text: I can't believe how many people on here are griping about Casa Video's late fees. Seriously? They charge you $.99 a day (might be more for new releases). Blockbuster used to claim your firstborn child if you returned a movie late. Casa's just extending your rental period for a slightly higher price. If you really truly cannot remember to return videos for weeks at a time, then please, I beg you, go to Netflix. I don't want you disappearing for two months with the movie I want to rent. As for Casa Video itself, this is the best video store I've ever been to, and I've been to some great video stores. If it's available on DVD, they generally have it on DVD, and if it's not, they have it on VHS. The few times I couldn't find a movie, I asked at the front desk and discovered I'd been looking in the wrong section. For the most part the employees know right where everything is, which is mind-blowing considering the number of movies they have. And, while the hyper-organized nature of the place can be a little disorienting, it's nice to be able to browse the "Giant Monsters" section. Or the "Derek Jarmin"section. Or the "Documentaries Addressing Social Issues" section. You could have a pretty amazing scavenger hunt without leaving the store. What else.... The DVDs are generally in good condition. The employees are all helpful, kind movie nerds. There's an unexpectedly vast soda selection. And free popcorn. And a video game section. And a porn section. They're open until 1am, and you can return movies right up until then on the day they're due. There's an after-hours drop box. There's some kind of rent-by-mail program, which I've never tried. And they link your account to your driver's license, instead of giving you another card to carry around. All told, Casa Video is one of the best businesses in Tucson, and one of the best video stores in the country. We're lucky to have it.
label: POS

text: I'm always looking for a local or semi-local restaurant with great food that my friends and I can go to that won't break the bank. Learning about Avalon Rustic Italian BYOB through co-workers and OpenTable (online reservation site), which listed the restaurant as a local favorite/treasure in West Chester; we decided that this would be our next destination. We made reservations through OpenTable and printed a coupon from restaurant.com, then waited eagerly for last night to taste some amazing Italian cuisine. Although not the fault of the restaurant, when I arrived into West Chester I had major difficulty parking. The restaurant does not have a lot to park in, the street parking around the restaurant was recently made residential parking by permit only, and the metered parking (15 minutes per quarter) which is at least 3 blocks away recently increased the time you have to pay the meter to 10pm. I found this frustrating as I was expecting a lot or to find close street parking as there was nothing on Avalon's website suggesting where to park or about the local parking changes. Again, this really isn't there fault but still frustrating to any non-local resident. Not prepared to park for several hours at a meter my husband and I walked several blocks to the restaurant hoping to get change for the meters. Upon arrival to the restaurant we were greeted by the hostess and informed her of our reservation. The restaurant was practically empty with only a table of three and the wait staff inside. We explained the parking situation to the hostess and were rudely told that they do not have change. Apparently they do not carry any quarters or anything to make change. Frustration level increasing my husband was instructed to walk to the closest laundry mat to see if he could get change there. I waited at the restaurant as we were meeting friends, and as I stood at the reception desk was gawked at for a few minutes while on the phone with other patrons making a reservation. While standing there I overheard her tell the patron that they were a CASH ONLY BYOB. This surprised me as we live in a plastic society and I don't know too many cash only establishments. It also surprised me as I didn't see this anywhere on their website. Once off the phone I was asked if I was going to wait outside or if I wanted to sit and wait for my party at our table. I first asked her about the cash only thing and she then asked how I made my reservation. I told her online and she said, "Oh, yeah we are cash only." I then proceeded to politely inform her that I planned on sitting and waiting for my party. Once seated I texted my husband as he was now going to stop at an ATM for cash. What I'm curious about is what tell telephone patrons that you are cash only but not online patrons or walk-ins that look at your webpage. Also, has does a cash only establishment not have change for patrons who have to park at meters? Eventually the parking and cash situation was resolved and my husband and friends arrived for our evening of Italian dining. Over all we found the establishment to just be okay. The atmosphere was quiet with a trendy looking interior. The menu was limited in selection and a little pricy for pasta and cheeses, especially for the small/average portions. Three different people stopped at our table to take care of us throughout our visit but never more than once so we were never really sure who our waiter was. We each ordered something different; my husband ordered the Butchers Bolognese which he described as being an attempted at a gourmet Hamburger Helper. Over all none of us where thrilled with our meals or the value compared to their cost. Recently my sister informed us of a new pasta bar opening in Downingtown, where Jasper's used to be. We were all excited about the new local dining option and couldn't wait to try it until we learned that it is an extension from this one. Now we are a little uncertain whether to try it or not. Tips for restaurant: Advertise on you webpage, not the menu posted on the web page that you are Cash Only, suggest parking areas for your patrons or have change available for the meters, and either increase the portion size or lower the price. Tips for patrons: bring cash, plan your parking in advance, and view menu prior to arrival Hopes for new pasta bar: a little less in price and more options on menu. Plus: this location has a lot and the street parking is not permit only.
label: NEG

text: Checked this place out on a whim last night with my friend. I kept putting it off because I eat at Mesh frequently (same owners) right down the street where I usually get, well, a burger. So I had a sneaking suspicion that it would be the exact same burger at Bru. Don't get me wrong, Mesh makes a good burger but I couldn't help but feel like Bru was Mesh's way of weeding the type of clientele out of their restaurant who come there to order a burger instead of a martini while at the same time keeping their money. I'll be damned if I am going to engage in culinary gentrification. The interior was nice and modern with a full bar. The music of choice was Sirius XM Hits of the Seventies so if you have ever wanted to eat a bacon burger to "Macho Macho Man" then this is your place. (Avoiding the low hanging fruit of the joke I want to make here in the interest of good taste) The ambiance worked though and I found myself unconsciously tapping my foot to Disco Inferno. Our waiter threw me for a loop by asking us if we had ever been there before and then promptly telling us what menu item not to order because it was terrible (for posterity, it was Peach Cobbler White Chocolate Bread Pudding). I found this to be an extremely odd form of salesmanship. "Welcome to Bru. Ever been here before?" (Me smiling) "No, I have not..." "Well, don't order the Peach Cobbler, I'm not a fan..." I spent way too much time thinking about the sales strategy behind this approach after he left the table with our drink orders. Was this some kind of Soviet Style psy-ops warfare? Was he attempting to build trust and a repoire with me as a customer by appearing to look out for my interests? Was he a man I could trust? Was the Peach Cobbler even a menu item or was it just there specifically so it would NOT be ordered? War is Peace. Freedom is Slavery. My room mate told me to shut the %(#& up and drink my iced tea. Downtown tap water (especially around the Mass Ave area) is really bad. Most restaurants use some form of filtered water so that their iced tea doesn't taste like it was strained through potting soil (MacNiven's and Bourbon St. being the worst perpetrators in terms of serving up a completely foul glass of iced tea). Bru's tea tasted normal so this boded well for the rest of the meal. I ordered the onion burger without cheese and my room mate asked if he could get the House Made Veggie Burger patty with the toppings of the Blazing Saddle burger (he is low maintenance). A minor gripe: fries are $2 extra so a $9 burger becomes $11. While I have no problem paying $11 for a burger with fries, the idea of paying $9 + $2 to ADD fries sits strangely with me. It's like, "Here are your biscuits for $2 and that'll be $1.50 for the gravy". The classic Burger and Fries are an American institution like Ketchup and Mustard, Bonnie and Clyde, Steak and um, Shake (have you ever thought about what it would be like to eat a huge sirloin steak with a strawberry shake? kind of weird.). You don't mess with an Institution (that's why I capitalized it). Give me the option in a little disclaimer-like line item at the bottom of the menu to deduct $2 from my meal if I decide to forego the fries (or shouId I say, sans FRENCH fries because I am cosmopolitan) but burger AND fries should be the default option. Stop playing mind games Bru. My burger was great and distinctly different from the one at Mesh. Well, as different as a dead animal can be I guess. (Seasoned to perfection!) I feel that I must acknowledge here that my dinner companion thought the veggie patty was terrible and only ate two bites of it before leaving its sad carcass torn in half on his plate. I tried to get him to just eat the patty itself with his fork thinking that perhaps it was the presentation and not the veggie burger itself. He indulged me before assuring me that, no, it was indeed the patty that was inedible. (I believe his exact words were "the consistency of a stool sample" which I found to be a bit harsh but with a cursory glance, more accurate than I cared to admit while still eating.) He became distraught that he was going to have to explain to the waiter why he had merely mangled his burger like Jack the Ripper while not actually eating any of it. Luckily, when the waiter returned to the table to collect our plates, our eyes met and there was an unspoken gentleman's agreement between us to just put the whole unpleasant business behind us. text: I think PATCO is swell. Yeah, I've ridden on better systems in Canada or Europe (DC is great too) but this is a pretty darn good high speed rail line from the Jersey burbs to center city Philly. Pros: I have yet to experience a late train other than once when a guy fell unconscious on the tracks at one of the stations and, like, I dunno, this one other time I don't really remember. If you are a freedom card holder it's a snap to get in and out of the stations and to refresh your cards value. Its way speedier than any other public transit into the city (from Jersey) if you live near enough to one of the stations. I have found the train cars to be clean enough to suit my tastes - usually only the odd newspaper or occasional soda bottle on one of the seats. They said they were going to start replacing the train cars but I kinda like the retro guacamole color scheme and the stainless steel "trainy" outside. I think the price is decent. I always feel safe in the stations, well lit parking lots and on the trains since there seems to be decent security folks (the port authority which owns the system has their own police force.) The staff on and off the trains have always been surprisingly pleasant to me. There's a nice lady who works rush hours at my station who is there to say hello and goodbye to everyone and help anyone who has a problem with their ticket or whatnot. Cons: Only a very limited number of the stations are handicapped accessible (elevators - since all stations are either above or below ground level) which I'm sure limits a lot of people's ability to utilize the line. I wonder how they get around the people with disabilities act in this regard but im sure there is some sort of loophole. It also is a super pain if you want to take your bike or a "granny cart" style shopping thingy with you, both of which I often want to do. The stations, especially on the Philly side, are usually quite dirty! Stick to standing up or sitting on one of the metal benches if you can get one - do not ever consider sitting on the floor - even if you are returning from a bender in the city; just steady yourself against a pole and try not to tip over. My little niece asked me why there was water on the stairs and I had to tell her it definitely was not water and definitely not to step in the puddle with her fliflops. I guess dirty stations in urban areas are not a particularly unexpected thing though, if they wanted to do one major thing to improve the line, it would be to increase the cleanliness quotient inside the stations. In most of the stations they have these posters that say renovations are being done on all the stations. The photos of what the stations are going to look like is all sleek and shiny. These signs have been up for years and there is not a single station that even remotely resembles the ones on the posters. The escalator in my station has been broken for about two months!!! Every day someone replaces the notice that says the escalator is being repaired because someone has scribbled some sarcastic (but true) funny statement about the situation. So, as an option to get into and out of the city its speedy, its cheap, its not gross and its convenient. In fact, I picked my current apartment partly based on how close it was to the PATCO station. During rush hour the cars are pretty packed so a lot of other folks must agree that its well worth it to take the train every day to and from work so it can't be all that bad. In fact, its usually quite pleasant!

text: i have held off on reviewing barbuzzo for several reasons. 1. i wanted to make sure the awesomeness wasn't a fluke. 5 times later, i've been assured it most certainly is not. 2. as a result of its consistent awesomeness, it's often difficult to get a table there. and the more i rave about this place, the more i hurt my chances of getting a rezzie 3. seriously, #2 again, for emphasis. but the conclusion is, that barbuzzo is too good not to share with people. i can say, without exaggeration, that it's easily in my top 5 faves in philly. and i'd even go as far as to say that it's usually top 1 or 2. what's good, you ask? i'd answer - EVERYTHING and it seems the menu items will have slight seasonal variations. but here are some specifics - my faves from the most recent dinner there. sheeps milk ricotta fresh made and drizzled with olive oil, sea salt and usually some sort of wine reduction, it's light, creamy, with just the slightest tang from the vin cotto that keeps bringing you back in for more. spread it over the toasted slice of bread that accompanies it and conversation will stop until all is consumed. summer risotto: caramelized torpedo shallows + asaparagus + favas creamy. rich. nutty. fightworthy. the portion of this is small (not really, but it will seem small because you'll want to eat more of it), but it's rich and hearty enough that it will sate you. if there are more than 2 of you, you might want to consider getting another. the 4 of us were scraping the plate. asparago pizza: shaved asparagus + pancetta + secret white sauce + fior di latte (a type of mozzarella made from cow's milk) + truffle + farm egg people used to rave about the uovo pizza, but this asparago (which i view as the evolution of its predecessor uovo), seriously elevates pizza. the pancetta has the perfect saltiness to balance the rich truffle flavor and the egg. whereas the guanciale in the previous version maybe provided bursts of salty flavor, the pancetta distributes it evenly over the entire pizza, really helping to bring it all together. i'm not sure what's in the 'secret' white sauce, but it may as well be crack because we really had to restrain ourselves from licking that pan clean as well. (ok, maybe we have a problem with licking our food plates) but really, it's that good. pan seared gnocci: smoked corn, trumpet mushrooms, tomatoes, prosciutto, grana everything gnocci should be - soft and plump delicious with the sweetness of the corn and earthiness of the mushrooms, the semi tart bite of tomatoes, and the salt of the meat keeping it interesting. caciocavallo stuffed meatballs: shortrib + pork + calabrian chile honestly. i don't even know what to say about this other than this is stuffed with unicorn magic, happiness and enlightenment. best meatballs ever. in life. on earth. this universe. trecce: twisty pasta + mushrooms + arugula + lemon-walnut pesto + ricotta originally, we ordered this as consolation to our vegetarian friend who couldn't eat any of the meaty things. but it turned out to be such a pleasant surprise. the lemon-walnut pesto was really bright and lovely with the mushrooms and arugula. definitely a dish you could keep eating w/out getting tired of it. and of course... the BUDINO. yes, forget your diet. just get one. or better yet, everyone at the table get your own. worth it. as for the other desserts, i will say, they were a bit disappointing. but learn the lesson here - never stray from the budino!

text: My husband has been a customer of Trumark financial since he opened his first account and I closed my account with Police and Fire federal credit union and joined Trumark when we married last year. I did not quite understand the extent that they would be changing their account fee structure but have been looking under fees on my statements just to make sure they did not apply to my accounts (We have two smaller accounts mostly for checking and on large account $10k plus for house expenses). Nothing has shown up under fees. I did a more detailed review of my April statement and noticed a strange charge on 4-30-12 marked "withdrawal ATM/POS fees" for $7.25 on my personal check account. When I called they explained that they have been charging us $0.25 for every Visa Debit transaction (not non-Trumark ATM withdrawals but actual "I bought it at Target and entered my Pin") transactions. I was appalled so I checked my husbands account. Long story short, we are paying over $20 a month to bank with Trumark and receiving next to nothing in interest on our savings. The fees are not shown in the fees section of my statement even though they are fees charged to you by Trumark and not anyone else which is extremely shady (and in my opinion the hidden fees are bordering on unethical). You expect this at a Wachovia or PNC (a bank that caters more to business accounts) but not at a community friendly credit union. I am switching back to Police and Fire where they actually pay me to use my debit!!!!!

text: I have been to this Continental multiple times. The food and service has always been fabulous. I went last night with my boyfriend. We started off with a pitcher of 21st Amendment Hell or High Watermelon. Mmmmmm. $29 is pricy for a pitcher of domestic (especially considering the German beers are considerably cheaper), but I love it so we had to have it. We always order the lobster mashed potatoes and the Korean pork tacos. THEY ARE BOTH DELCIOUS. And last night we thought we'd try some new things and also ordered the cheesesteak eggrolls. ((They were also really good.)) The reason, however, that I am giving this restaurant ONE star and will not be back for a very long time -- if ever again -- is due to the hygiene of the restaurant and its overall lack of hospitality management or customer service "skills." My boyfriend and I had both polished off the tacos and moved along to some lobster mash (let me reiterate: MMMMMMM with capital M's). Then I branched off and tried an eggroll. When I'm reaching for more lobster mash I realize there is a long, nappy, curly hair buried in there. Or maybe not buried but actually hanging from the potatoes off the side of the plate. The manager had been over a few seconds prior and we had told her everything was fine. After finding the hair, I immediately called her back over. She apologized and asked if we wanted more. My appetite was gone at this point but the lobster mash IS delicious so I told her to pack one up to go. My server, Kendall, came back over and asked if we wanted any more drinks or dessert to which we both declined. Afterwards, she told us that "in case we didn't know," the manager was taking the lobster mash off the check. Ummm...Thank God? I really had thought this would be a given. Unfortunately for Kendall, this really just made things worse. Honestly, all I wanted was an apology. Regardless of if she had anything to do with the hair being in the food or not, an apology should have been the first thing she said to me. Do I want to order dessert? IS IT FREE? No? Ok then, fuck off. When the fresh lobster mash came out we also got the check. All that was taken off was the lobster mash. Not even a round of the several that we had. No free dessert. No further apologies. I found it hard to believe that a Stephen Starr restaurant could be so cheap when it came to reimbursing diners who have had a negative experience. I mean poor service is one thing but when I'm actually sickened and frightened at the thought of eating more of their food, I draw the line. Understandably the lobster mash is taken off the check, but with that hair comes the idea that I now don't want to eat any of the entire plate of eggrolls I still have left and can't even consider ordering dessert. If the issue had been handled more effectively and in a manner which truly takes hospitality into account, I wouldn't be writing this today. Hair in the food -- Strike 1 Insufficient apology -- Strike 2 Cheap reimbursement -- Strike 3 Continental Old City -- Yooooou'reeee outtttaaaa herrrrrre!!!

For such an elaborate piece, even the simplest mistakes can add to the character. When in Creve Couer, come check it out. text: Maybe it's because I don't stay at fancy schmancy hotels on the regular, but I have pretty modest expectations when it comes to hotels. I think some people are far too picky and want everything to be the Ritz. For under $200 a night, you will not be sleeping in the lap of luxury. But you will find a nice, clean room that is a decent size, friendly staff, free wi-fi, and an indoor pool. And a very comfy bed, which seems to be standard for Holiday Inns. They also seem to have made some upgrades since I was last here in 2009 - new paint jobs, new carpet in the hallways, that sort of thing. It just feels "newer." The major bonus to this Holiday Inn is its location. You are within walking distance of everything in the French Quarter (and Frenchman Street, if you don't mind a hike). You are also right on the edge of the CBD (Central Business District) and can walk to Harrah's, the Aquarium, the businesses on Canal Street, the St. Charles streetcar, and a plethora of other wonderful New Orleans things. Royal Street is also one of the quieter areas of the Quarter, so you are pretty insulated from the Bourbon Street chaos but still close enough to partake if that's your thing. Yes, there can be some sketchy characters around the hotel. This is partly due to the liquor store that is directly across the street. But if you have an issue with sketch then what are you doing in New Orleans? I never felt unsafe while going to and from the hotel, and we were out at all hours of the day and night. Also, if you (or in my case, your spouse) happen to be a government employee they have an AWESOME rate. You will also get free parking (it's regularly $26.00/day. Yikes. But you don't really need a car in New Orleans.) But when you get right down to it, New Orleans is such an amazing city that you shouldn't be spending time in the hotel! Take advantage of the great location and laissez le bon temps rouler!
label: POS

text: The itinerary for most tourists in NOLA is pretty standard: a photo session in Jackson Square (http://www.yelp.com/biz/jackson-square-new-orleans), a stroll through the French Quarter, a little perusing at the French Market (http://www.yelp.com/biz/french-market-new-orleans), a bite of some beignets at Cafe Du Monde (http://www.yelp.com/biz/caf%C3%A9-du-monde-new-orleans-5), and a hurricane here at Pat O'Brien's. Like any good bar, there are a number of delicious liquid concoctions worth considering, but a hurricane is about Louisiana as it gets. For folks literally coming here for the first time, be sure to arrive sometime in the afternoon and ready to drink. The patio area is a gorgeous spot to lounge and take in the sweet southern sunshine while sipping on a sugary sweet hurricane that run at about $8 each. Though girly on paper, these babies are smooth yet potent enough to get even the biggest lush on his/her tippy toes after one giant glass. I think for locals, Pat O'Brien's is a lot more than just hurricanes. It is a place to people watch, make requests at the popular piano bar, its mingling in the courtyard, and being a patron of one of the finest venues the city has to offer. The service is top notch, most of the bartenders have been around the block or two and know how to make a mean drink while keeping their customers smiling. Beware of coming out here for holidays like New Year's or even St. Patty's. The crowds are fierce and similarly to Mardi Gras, it's bumper to bumper human traffic. I personally like coming out to Pat O'Brien's during weekdays, the vibe is relaxing, the people are laid back, and it's nice to be able to just take a hurricane on the road and stroll around the rest of the Big Easy.

text: My husband and I are from Austin, so we really love Texas BBQ. We're not really experts in pulled pork or deep south BBQ. We were really intrigued when we found this place, which is only a minute away from where we live. We shared their 2 meat combo platter and got the baby back ribs and the sliced brisket with the carolina sauce, plus the sweet potato fries and cole slaw, which came out to a little under $15. The store layout is similar to a local pizza joint-- not a good place to eat in IMO (although there are tables and chairs) but great for takeout. I read an article they had hanging on their wall about the restaurant, and it said that Fletcher's was a restaurant that featured a sampling of all different types of BBQ- brisket from Texas, plus ribs and pulled pork from other parts of the south. They also have several types of sauce-- again, one Texas-inspired, another carolina, and a third that I don't remember. It's family-run by a family that decided to pursue their dreams away from corporate America. I'm always excited to try out local businesses. They said that they had been open for about 2 years. Being from Texas, I had a few expectations of what a BBQ place should be like, but it could just be that people do BBQ differently in different places. The menu features chopped and sliced brisket, ribs, pulled pork and pulled chicken, plus a few other things like a smoked whole or half chicken. Interestingly, they don't have any sausage, which to me should be a staple. Their sides are also a mix of different places-- cole slaw, sweet potato fries, collard greens, tater tots, mac and cheese, and baked beans.... but no potato salad, which again is a staple down in Texas. The thing that bugged me the most was that there was no sweet tea to be found, but I'd rather take a place with no sweet tea and great BBQ than a place with bad BBQ and great sweet tea. No free side items like pickles or onions were available either. The brisket was sliced generously, and not thinly. it's wasn't melt-in-your-mouth but it wasn't super chewy either. My favorite part was that it wasn't too charred on the outside but had nice darkness to it. The baby back ribs are fall-off-the-bone. I can see why the ribs got rave reviews from other yelpers. I wish there was more sauce on the meat, but that's probably a personal preference, as I'm used to there being extra tubs of sauce to dunk your meat in as opposed to the sauce only being poured directly onto the meat. I really liked that the meat was served on top of a delicious buttered piece of Texas toast. Delicious! I'm so glad to find a place that does BBQ well right here in Abington and that I don't need to drive 1600 miles to get it. It's not pure Texas BBQ but both my husband and I really enjoyed our meal. We'll be back, and next time we'll try the pulled pork and some different sides!

text: I really wanted to enjoy this stay in Reno. I thought that this hotel was highly rated on Yelp and Tripadvisor, so I intentionally deviated from my normal hotel selections and stayed here. I thought that it was neat how they replaced a check-in attendant with a kiosk (it's the wave of the future). The room layout is spacious, with a large living area (tradeoff: sink + bathroom are smaller). Surprisingly there were a couple of specific things that will have me stay at another hotel the next time I'm here. First, climate control was horrible. The thermostat was near the front door of the room, all the way on the other side of the heater. Combine this with the fact that the bed is literally 2 feet away from the heater, and you'll notice that temperature fluctuates a lot. Add the fact that the heater is loud, and it makes for a very unpredictable night of sleep. Secondly, the showerhead in the room was horrible. There were multiple settings on the showerhead, and it was either a harsh direct narrow spray, or a very low pressure drizzle. Yes, I showered fine but it was not the relaxing type of shower I had experienced at other hotels. Third, the breakfast area was too cold. Wind drafts in the dining area kept me feeling a tad bit chilly, and the food got cold easily. Might I suggest to management that food workers use gloves to handle food, especially when moving food items from tray to tray. Ironically, I had a much better time with the basic rooms in Silver Legacy + El Dorado in Reno (and I don't like the smoke or the gambling!)

Like when the one guy tried to say that the barren landscape was symbolism for this and that. Joan told him he was wrong, but did it so right. He was not offended at all. Our group stuck together for the whole tour, and she went over the allotted time, but we told her it was okay. She is so enthusiastic and knowledgeable. text: I really wish I could give them more stars! The idea is good but the price is too high for the client service the I received. If you're not familiar with their business model, these guys will help you set up a self-directed IRA and an LLC. The IRA then invests in the LLC to buy investments like real estate or precious metals. The LLC documents have to contain special language in order for the IRA to invest in it, which is why you can't just buy one off of the internet. This investment strategy is somewhat uncommon but growing in popularity. The relative rarity of the investment strategy means that the companies that do offer the service can charge a premium. I set one up through my attorney before I learned about these guys and he charged around $3,000 for the privilege. I then set up an IRA/LLC through Guidant for both myself and my husband and it was a little bit less expensive. PROS: * They are familiar with the process and fill out all the paperwork for you * They send you the documentation with clear instructions on execution * You can pay for the service plus filing fees with your credit card CONS: * Their client service was sub-par. For the amount of money I was paying, I expected really great client service, but the associate assigned to my case would harangue me for the information. And I don't mean she would call me up and ask how it was going to check in. She would literally call up and say "Where is the paperwork? When are you getting it back to us?" Every interaction with her was painful. * They submitted some paperwork to the State with a mis-keyed address, even after I had pointed out the error on Federal paperwork. Their response was "Oh that's too bad, this is how you fix it." So their review process isn't great and they don't even have the decency to apologize. * Their sales group is pushy. Once you get on their radar, they will be calling you EVERY DAY until you sign up. Not kidding even a little. * They e-mail you all of the final documents and expect you to print them out and put them in a nice little binder. Even NOLO will put your documents together in a binder, and I'm only paying $299 for that service. If I'm paying a little south of $6k, I would expect a dang binder and some fancy tabs - not much to ask. When I asked them if they could assemble it for me, the client service lead refused. Google maps indicated there was an Office Max less than a mile away from their office, so THAT wasn't the problem. These aren't the only guys out there that do this sort of work - I was unimpressed with the client service experience for the price that they charge. I'd recommend looking around - I bet you can find something better.
label: NEG

The pavement is great for bicycles, people-watching and folks who need an easier walk, while the trails are extensive enough to provide that much-needed furlough from humanity that I so craved. text: I think the owner was having a bad day yesterday. I was also eating there, and had a similar experience. Usually when I see these hyperbolic WORST EXPERIENCE EVER posts I assume the reviewer is wildly exaggerating, but in this case, this all really happened. A: The food Not bad, not great. The rice is dry, and the sesame chicken was a bit weak, but the steak I got was pretty good and the pot stickers we got as an appetizers were awesome. B: The place It's trying VERY hard to be an upscale Asian fusion restaurant, and it looks good I guess. Certainly fancier than anything else you're gonna find at the park mall. C: The service Yikes. It's really creepy how closely my experience mirrored the customer below. First, my waiter repeated everything instead if writing it down. Okay, fair enough, if he remembers what I ordered. He comes back (after a LONG wait incidentally) with the wrong food though. I didn't want to be a total jerk so I nicely asked if I could get it sent back and the right food sent out. The waiter takes it back (and did apologize) but came back 5 minutes later asking me again to confirm what I ordered. When I did, the waiter took a copy if the menu back to the kitchen, acting like he needed proof for them that this menu item exists. He also explained the runner took some the wrong dishes to the wrong tables, which is how this happened apparently. He then comes back another TEN minutes later to apologize more, explaining that the owner is back cooking because someone called out, and he's furious, etc. Okay, I don't see how that's any of my business or concern, but it explains the delay I guess. Another ten minutes later, no food. My girlfriend is done eating by now, I still haven't been served. So I flag the waiter down and say I'd prefer to just get the check at this point, as I don't want to make her wait. The waiter apologized more, mentions again that the owner is freaking out, and that several tables got the wrong food. He mentions he'll void the check, which isn't what I asked for, my girlfriends food was fine, but whatever. The waiter comes back, almost in tears now, and asks if there's any way he can convince me to stay, because the owner is now blaming HIM for the screwup and is going to take the check out of the waiters pay. Obviously I dont want that, so (feeling horribly uncomfortable) I say sure. The waiter thanks me, says he's going to put in his two weeks tomorrow because the owner is a lunatic, and says the food will be right out. At this point, I just want to wolf down my food and get out of here. The waiter is clearly terrified and upset, my girlfriends been done for 20 minutes, and I just want out. The waiter comes back, and the steak is raw in the middle. Like not even a little cooked. So against all my wishes, I have to tell the waiter I can't eat it. At this point, the owner himself comes over and glared at me and goes "what's wrong". Not yelling exactly, but pissed. I tell him its raw. He responds with "well you wanted it fast". Then he takes the plate back to the grill and storms off. My girlfriend is now also fairly upset, and asks if we can just get of boxed and leave. So when the waiter comes back, I ask if we can do that. He says sure, but then instead of grabbing a box, he spends five minutes explaining at length that the owner is a psycho, he's going to quit, etc.. I obviously believed him now, but man, I just want OUT, please go get my box. Eventually he gets the box, we pay, and just kind of flee. The food was good enough, but its clear from other reviews and from how he acted that day that the owner is a really awful, awful person. It takes an impressive amount of incompetence to personally cause the patrons of a restaurant YOU OWN to flee in terror. I can't recommend strongly enough to stay away from this place. When something goes wrong you're out of luck if the owner himself is the problem.

text: Every now and then when my wife says "I don't feel like cooking, where are we going to dinner?" the name Bertucci's pops into my head. I'm very forgetful, so it must be my subconscious reminding me how much I love their rolls and pizza. When we go out with our four kids in tow, it's a big deal and a very rare event, and we want to go to a place where we know we will like the food. The freshly made rolls that are served still warm are amazing. Immediately after the waiter drops the rolls off, my mouth is watering uncontrollably while I break open the crispy crust to reveal the soft fluffy interior, then dipping (well, dredging really) the hunk of bread into the oil. There are not many things that make me struggle more with self control than trying to refrain from having a 3rd, 4th, 5th roll before my dinner has even arrived. Then the pizza comes. I almost always order the Margherita. The sauce is always delicious and is perfectly accompanied by fresh mozzarella cheese and basil. I order the individual (which is plenty of food for one, especially after the complimentary rolls) but I think I could polish off a large. I'm not the biggest fan of most chain restaurants, but I'm rarely disappointed when I visit Bertucci's. Most of the time I leave stuffed and extremely satisfied.

She was a little bit bummed, but the server was very accommodating in making a substitution. The food took a little while to come out. When it finally did, I was told that they were making more fresh whipped cream (for the lemon corncakes) and that it would be ready shortly. It finally arrived about fifteen minutes later, when I only had one corncake left. Again, not really a dealbreaker, but slightly disappointing. In addition, I also know a bit about BMWs. First, on a stock BMW 3 series, there is something called an alignment pin that is there from the factory! This pin holds the strut in a particular location so you can't change the camber. If you do remove the pin, which is only allowed by BMW for excessive camber problem (such as hitting a curb, accidents, etc.), then you could remove it but it creates another problem because the strut is now able to move in the future... throwing off your alignment. So why do these engineers put these pins in there for the first place? So you don't touch the camber if you car doesn't have a problem! The technician who worked on my car, is a joke. First, he selected the damn wrong profile for my BMW. I walked into the bay and told him to choose 3 series, 18" WITH sports package. A sports package suspension has much more aggressive setup than a non-sports suspension. What this means is that the "center" of each alignment criteria is different. On a 3 series coupe 335i, the rear camber is center at -1.8 but on a stock non-sport suspension, it is center at -1.4. See what I'm talking about? The idiot technician decides to choose the standard suspension. He wouldn't let me scroll down to tell him to choose the "Sports Perf Suspension". How do I know it exists in the system? Because I just got a free alignment check in the other RapidCheck system 5 minutes ago! That profile (template) exists! This guy has NO CLUE about BMW's. Next, this guy decides to pop my hood and begins to hammer my strut. I told him WTF are you doing? He wouldn't respond. He was trying to remove the alignment pin. I told him to stop, and I told him to NOT touch that pin. He told me to relax, he knows what he's doing, he's got 3 years of auto experience, blah blah...and that I shouldn't be telling him how to do his job. I was not telling him how to do his job, I simply told him NOT to change the front camber and to leave that pin alone! All the alignment shops I've been to in the past, have never touched the front camber and that alignment pin!! Under no circumstances do one need to remove that pin unless you modified your car, or had a significant accident, or bent some suspension parts. If I did bent some suspension, one should replace those suspension instead. After calling the manager over to tell him to select the right profile, he quickly finished up, leaving my car in a sub-par aligned condition. I took my car to another Sears in Costa Mesa to check the alignment and it was STILL off! I decided to go to an independent shop, got it fixed. Then went to Sears in Pasadena and finally the alignment is all correct. AVOID this place at all costs and do not bring your car here for an alignment. Just bring your car here for the free alignment checks and then get the hell out of there!

text: Just as every supervillian has their superhero counterpart, so it goes with college venues in St. Louis. There are two private universities in St. Louis that people pay attention to: Wash U and SLU (I'll throw in Webster if we're allowed halfsies). As far as academics are concerned, there's really no comparison (sorry Jesuits), but as far as I'm concerned, the two are on equal footing on just about every other level. So in my mind, it's fair to compare and contrast the two schools on the same plane. Not every university has its own music venue booked and run by students, and for good reason. 90% of the time, it's a shitshow. Students are constantly rotating in and out of the organization, no one can keep anything organized, the students who attend are assholes (if they attend at all), there are security issues, it's hard to get money for halfway decent bands to perform, etc. Hey, I understand. I've been to enough college-run shows to know how the system works. Most of the time, you're lucky if the show goes off without a hitch. That's why attending a venue like The Billiken Club is such a breath of fresh air. In the realm of university-run music venues, it is the exception. First off, all the shows are free to everyone, including the general public. Other places try to make it free for students and charge non-students, but it becomes very difficult to control and ends up becoming even more confusing than before (besides, how much money do these venues make by charging the public? A couple hundred bucks? I assume that money ultimately goes to seeing how much Popov vodka it can buy.) In addition to being free, the entering/ticketing process is really smooth. The people at the door are much friendlier and easy-going than they have a right to be, and it lends itself to a positive atmosphere. They card you and slap a wristband on you if you're over 21 because unlike nearly any other college campus I've been on....there's alcohol served! (+1 for the Jesuits). This is a godsend for people who want a beer or two before the show, and it partially forgoes the typical college attitude of "get drunk before we go out" that sometimes leads to violent drunkenness. The layout itself is pretty nice. Yes, this is a cafeteria by day, and yes, it's in the basement of the student center, but it's a newer, large space with relatively good sight lines. The support beams are all graffiti'd up, you can pop outside to smoke if you wish, the bar area is clearly separated from the music so you don't have to scream over the band, and there's an area separated by a wall where you can actually sit down for a few minutes and take a break if needed. It's actually designed very well and feels as much like a real club as can be expected. It seems kind of like the university takes a hands off approach when it comes to managing the space, as long as the students don't screw anything up and clean up after themselves. The music bookings are pretty good as well. They have a tendency to get bands that are on the way up but haven't quite hit it big yet. Whoever selects the bands to book must know their stuff, because it appeals to my inner musicphile. The crowd is mostly well-behaved, and security is usually pretty leanient, as long as you're not doing something real dumb. The sound system is also a step above what I usually experience for clubs this size (under 500 people). It's clear someone was able to secure some university money for the setup, and made good with it. The Billiken Club is a very good place to listen to music in St. Louis. It's not as good as other places, but it's eons ahead of it's doppelganger at Wash U, The Gargoyle. You can read my review of that dungeon if you'd like, but save yourself the time and just check out this place instead. If you go once, you may find yourself looking for a reason to go back.

text: Crystal BBQ Noodle House used to be the Jasmine Noodle House - in fact, the original signage on the purple awning over the door remains, with a Crystal BBQ sign in the window. We were not sure at first we were even in the right place. Upon entering, our olfactory senses were filled with the smell of barbecue meat, and we saw a table of people cooking their own food on one of those little portable stoves. Were we in a noodle house or a barbecue restaurant? Our menus indicated noodle house. The majority of the menu were the typical dishes expected in a Vietnamese noodle house, especially pho (noodle soup) and vermicelli bowls. I opted for a rare beef pho, while my co-worker had a steamed chicken pho. For appetizers, she chose a half order of shrimp salad rolls while I had green onion cakes. Our appetizers were brought while I sipped my jasmine tea, rich in flavour. My onion cakes were crispy and delicious. My co-worker raved about her salad rolls. We both looked around and kept admiring the beautiful decor of the dining area. With anticipation, we looked forward to our soups arriving. After a short while, two steaming bowls of pho were placed before us. My bowl was big enough, but did not seem to have as much broth as I am used to. There were loads of noodles though, and I dipped my spoon in to taste the broth. Alas, there was not much flavour - the only seasoning I could really taste was salt. I would have put some of the herbs served typically served to the side, but all we were given was a tiny plate with a few sprouts, a lime wedge, and a leaf that I had never seen before when having pho. The meat tasted good enough - all six slices of it, which were already cooked through by the time the bowl arrived at the table (rare beef pho is supposed to be served rare). Colleen had a similar experience with her soup. Although she doused the broth with salt and soy sauce, she commented that it was flavourless. The tiny shreds of chicken tasted good - almost too good. We suspected they were processed or laden with MSG. Neither of us finished our soup, nor took home the leftovers. The prices are slightly higher than other noodle houses, so I could not understand why the portions of meat were so small. While paying the bill, our server explained that they had kept the lunch menu from the previous owners, and the evening menu was barbecue. Judging from the rich, meaty smells that greeted us, I am willing to bet the barbecue is not bad - however, given how bad our soups were, neither of us are willing to return to find out. Here is a suggestion: if you take over a restaurant, don't try to be all things to all people. Either change the menu to what you do best, or learn how to prepare the existing menu items properly. Any pho lover would have been disappointed by their meal - we sure were.

text: I stopped in Pita Jungle for the first time today for lunch. I drive by daily on my way to work and considered going here several times, but the prices always steered me away. Most lunch dishes are $9-$11, and to me this is high to pay for lunch. After today's visit though, I will most definitely be back. The portions more than make up for the price- everything is HUGE. I ordered the tomato garlic chicken, and I could easily eat my leftovers for tomorrow's lunch and then some. After only eating half my meal, I'm still full 4 hours later. FOOD: My chicken was fantastic. It's a special so I don't know how long it will be on the menu. The chicken itself was thinly sliced, but still very moist and tender. The garlic potatoes and garlic sauce it came with made my mouth water. The spinach was nicely cooked. Hard to serve cooked spinach at a restaurant without it being too wilty so I was impressed. The other ladies at my table ordered the Mediterranean Salad, which looked very fresh and delicious and was huge, the Chipotle Black Bean Burger which again was a very generous portion and no complaints from her, and the third at our table ordered the Spinach Pasta Salad which she said was fabulous. For an appetizer, we shared the jalapeno cilantro hummus, and it was delicious. My only complaint on the food was the dessert. We ordered the creme brulee which was slightly overcooked because the custard part was too thick. It still tasted OK though. The iced teas are flavored but unsweetened - another nice and somewhat rare offering. I highly recommend the kiwi, very refreshing. SERVICE: The service was a bit slow (we came in after the lunch rush and there was only one girl covering the whole place, and to top it off she was training another waitress, but she did very well considering). Even with only one waitress to the whole place the food still came out pretty fast, and our drinks were always refilled promptly. At the end, the waitress came around and gave us all to-go cups freshly filled with iced tea. This was a really nice touch that I really appreciated. It was nice to go back to work with some yummy kiwi tea. SUMMARY: I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a fresh alternative to all the greasy lunch pits in the area. The food is tasty and won't leave you with a feeling of guilt. Try the hummus and flavored iced teas- you won't regret it!! [A note about me: I've traveled around the world more than once and eaten everywhere from the smallest, sleepiest taco shop in San Felipe to pizza in China (yes, they have pizza in China and yes, there were corn and peas on it) to five-star restaurants in Vegas and everything in between. I say this because I've found many Tucsonans don't know how to eat, and don't know what good service is (no offense, not everyone has had the opportunities I have). That being said, you can assume my reviews are legit. I hold everyone to a very high standard and don't settle for crap. ]
