THAT particular young woman LEFT this location earlier this year and after dealing with the rest of the staff and having one lady (who I later found out was the DOCTOR and owner of the place) snidely tell me that she did not care if I had a prescription, it was more than six months old and I needed a new exam if I "expected" to buy glasses from them. Yes, you read that correctly. #1 - my prescription, at the time, was just at FIVE months old. I had an exam done in the beginning of April of THIS year and moved HERE in the MIDDLE of the month. I went into this location in September....so, five months. #2 - IF I EXPECTED TO BUY GLASSES FROM THEM? No, I expected to be treated with respect being as I was CHOOSING to purchase something from them and had $ to burn on this above what my insurance would have covered. Needless to say, I stormed out, my friend was very upset that he had been lied to about the person he wanted to help me still being there, and I found somewhere else to go for my services. And the upside is that when I brought the business cards to my friend, he was ecstatic because the lady that helped me with my glasses at the new place was the VERY person he was trying to get me to see to begin with. I found EVERYBODY at Eye Works un-professional, rude and snide. Sorry J M that I didn't post before - I may have been able to save you the trouble.
label: NEG

text: Tat Tits and Trash Bourbon Street gives you exactly what it promises. Mile high daiquiris, mile wide crowds and every club blasting music, side by side, volume set to 11. Cheap garish signs and advertising block beautiful architecture. Unknown liquids puddle and steep in the heat creating smells that rival the streets of Bangkok. The frenetic race to reach alcohol oblivion permeates the atmosphere. Christine's tip: Walk one block south of Bourbon St. to Royal Street. Here you will find local street musicians (don't confuse "street" for amateurs, these cats smoke!) , art galleries, cafes and higher quality tourist shops. If you're lucky you'll catch a fireworks show being shot over the majestic Mississippi River.
label: NEG

text: I've been here a number of times and the SO is obsessed with their tortas. (Read: OBSESSED, haha) Decor: They've remodeled this place and now they actually have a legit fenced in patio with a roof on it- very pretty. It's funny, because inside it's more of a fast, cheap Mexican restaurant decor with no decorations at all. There are tables and also bar stools along the sides of the restaurant- not a bad idea for extra seating. Service: Always fast and prompt. If there's a wait, good luck. Food: Of course, I have had their tortas, more specfically, their torta al pastors! They really are scrumptious with a little bit a spice in it, albeit a bit oily (but then again, who gets healthy Mexican food?). I actually like their tongue one better because it isn't as oily and I smother on that green and red sauce on it. :) Yummm. Bad thing is that they do not have alcohol. They have this non-alcoholic beer... sigh, they need to get on that and get a liquor license or something. For the price we paid for this "OK" hotel, I expect better customer service. Most, not all, staff were either rude or rushed. The rooms were "ok" and the resort itself was pretty nice. text: At the risk of being tarred and feathered by all the other yelpers who love this place, I offer the following advice about eating at Galatoires: DON'T DO IT. Just slowly back away. I must add we were warned not to go by our waiter at breakfast on Jackson Square. First of all, my husband Bruce and I were extremely excited about our first visit to Galatoires. We love traditional NOLA restaurants and were really looking forward to our visit. We had an 8pm reservation and were seated fairly promptly That's basically when the problems began. Our waiter finally made his first appearance after about 7 minutes. Not good in a high end restaurant. While we were waiting, we were stunned by the noise level. This place was louder than any restaurant I've ever been too. This is supposed to be fine dining? Finally when the waiter shows up, we take our cue from other yelpers and ask him what he recommends tonight. His answer was a shrug of the shoulders then he mumbled something about pompano and some other dishes but it was so f*****g noisy I couldn't hear a word of it. He appeared totally bored with the whole situation. So, we share the shrimp remoulade appetizer which was just awright. Bruce gets the shrimp creole which was so/so. (I can make better and I don't consider myself a gourmand) and I order the softshell crabs which are on the menu but alas are out of season (major disappointment since I had them the night before at another restaurant and they were just fine). I end up with the crabmeat something or other with spinach and hollandaise sauce. It was cold when it arrived. I sent it back, it came back identically cold. WTF? I told the waiter not to even bother bringing it back again. I ordered a 13.00 glass of red wine that tasted like the bottle had been opened a week ago. Not accceptable. That got sent back too. And I hate complaining in restaurants but jeez louise! I guess if you are a local they treat you well there. We must have had tourist written all over our faces (yes we were dressed up, husband had on jacket and slacks) but it is obvious if you are just visiting you are not worth the trouble. Huge disappointment. Much better places to eat in the area.
label: NEG

text: Been going to various Lee's locations for years. I ordered a cheese steak hoagie. Lee's rolls are awful - they're very airy, no substance to them. Also, there's was not enough meat on the cheese steak hoagie, and the meat that is there just squeezes out the sides. Also, the meat was chopped. For years they did not chop their meat - not sure what their other locations do. There was also hardly any lettuce, tomato or onion on it. It's also too expensive for an average hoagie with smaller portions. The girls behind the counter were pleasant, the place was clean - but it was freezing cold in there. I'll stick w/ Primo's, Cosimo's, Sarcone's, Di Bruno's or any of the places in Reading Terminal Market.

text: To preface this, I didn't grow up in the south, so didn't have the pleasure of dining at Shoney's until relatively recently, upon moving to TN. As such, my view of Shoney's might be slightly different than it would be had I been raised in the area. Now for the review. I like this place. I've had brunch their twice, the buffet each time. It's cheap -- maybe $7, and it's on a road named "interstate Dr," so it's not going to be gourmet. If you want gourmet, pay a few extra bucks and travel up the street to five points. If you want something that's fast, filling, cheap, and unlimited, come to Shoney's. This place is surprisingly well run. The two times I went it wasn't too busy, and it seems clean and fresh. I've only had their buffet, so I can't comment on other menu items, but for $7, it's quite a deal. As a bonus, you don't have to wait around for long to get seated, so it's good if you want to get food in a hurry. The coffee isn't bad, either. This place is also great for people watching. The people who dine at Shoney's are an interesting bunch, and because of the location there's a lot of variety. Lots of cute kids, too. Overall, a good place to eat if you want to stuff our face with breakfast food and be on your way.

text: So awesome! It took us about 2 months to finally make it here after hearing about it from a friend and oh how I regret all of that wasted time! It certainly won't take another 2 months for us to go back, that's for sure! For apps, we had hummus & tzatziki served with HOT pita bread --- sooo good! Next time I'll ask if I can buy a container of tzatziki to take home. During the apps, Chef George sent out a huge platter of fresh hand cut fries for our kids which they appreciated very much. My husband had the moussaka, I had the grilled octopus, one of our boys had the chicken sandwich (off the lunch menu which they allowed us to order from) and our other son had pasta with marinara sauce (special order). The portions are huge. There was so much chicken on my son's chicken sandwich (in pita bread)! Everything was delicious. My grilled octopus was fresh and cooked perfectly. My husband loved the moussaka, perfectly seasoned & very hearty. We got the honey yogurt cake for dessert. It's served warm with fresh homemade yogurt on the side. Again, the serving was huge!! It was delicious, very light and moist. It's a very homey, comfortable restaurant. George came out a couple of times and chatted with us about our meal and the restaurant. Our server (Abby according to the receipt) was great! Definetely a hidden gem!
label: POS

text: Usually great food, consistently good service. Good focus on local beers (love the rotating taps of Fountain Square Brewing Company and Triton) A couple of complaints: As with any restaurant, the Red Lion kitchen will prepare stuff ahead and reheat it once ordered. The common problem here is the reheating part. I eat here a lot and more often than not the mashed potatoes are cold. I mean...really cold. A few others items I have had were lukewarm, most recently the chicken tikka masala. A good dish, if a bit bland, but it was not hot at all. The fries are consistently bad here, but they do have an excellent spicy curry dip to take away the soggy, burnt flavor of the fries. I would recommend going to a thicker fry and not keeping them up as long. They often taste like they have been reheated in the oil. Those complaints aside, they really do have good food and good recipes! Great atmosphere, very cozy and welcoming.

text: This place is good as fast food goes but it's still fast food. I can make better Mexican food at home. And many authentic Mexican restaurants can make real Mexican food quickly without it being fast food. What's lacking? Multiple things: * The freshness of the ingredients...they're okay, not bad, just not super fresh. * The salsas are not hot enough. The medium has almost no detectable heat and the hot is what I'd call somewhere between mild and medium. * None of the ingredients stand out as amazing. Everything is just a tad bland: the cheese, the rice. * The meat is too salty...perhaps to mask low-quality meat? * The guacamole is insanely expensive..$1.19...I can buy a whole avocado for that price. Give me a break. I can understand charging maybe 79 cents but charging well over a dollar is price gouging. I think it's sad that these restaurants persist when there are so many hole-in-the-wall Mexican places that offer fresher, tastier food for cheaper.
label: NEG

text: There's a reason why the substantial parking lot of this run-down diner car is always filled with taxis. For good Middle Eastern/South/Central Asian (not sure exactly which region Pakistan is considered part of) food, follow the Middle Eastern/South/Central Asian cabbies. I know Pakistanis from New Jersey who gladly pay the $4 bridge toll to eat at this restaurant. I've tried just about everything here, and pretty much everything is solid. Some things are better than others, and some things (like salmon or chicken breast) can be a little dry at times. However, everything is really flavorful, and all the platters (~$11) come with rice, a huge slab of naan, a small serving of meh salad-from-a-bag and a veggie side. Each platter is a meal and a half for me. I'm partial to the lamb (both chops and kebab), the tandoori chicken is great, and their post-Ramadan whole fried chicken deal is pretty good. The spicy green sauce that comes with every platter is clutch, so ask for extra. For hearty homestyle Pakistani food-from-the-grill, Kabobeesh is the way to go.
label: POS

text: We were there for lunch on Saturday the 12th of March. I was a regular, not sure if I'll ever go back now, who rarely orders because Joe, along with a couple other servers, knows my order so well. One of two dishes, 10 star, tofu - as I am a vegetarian. When our food was dropped at our table my dish, Pud Thai, had shrimp in it. I asked the old lady if there was chicken in it and her reply was, "well if you didn't order it without meat then there will be chicken in it" For the record I ordered it as a vegetarian dish, and who does this lady think she is? We ordered another plate, with tofu this time, and my girlfriend waited for my food to be prepared while her's got cold. Our drinks were never topped off, the hostess had a snotty attitude (not the first time for her) and it wasn't that busy of a Saturday afternoon. When the bill came, we paid for three plates of food, and left. I hope the owner enjoyed that extra twelve dollars tacked onto our bill. I have never had such horrible service in that place, or anywhere else in Reno for that matter. Joe did his best but as the only server on, with little to no support from the other two, but no customer should have to deal with the BS that came out of that old lady's mouth.

text: Need a little decompression time or a few hour vacation? Then sprint on over to the Black Pearl in Old Hickory, TN. I swear you will think that you just dropped anchor in Panama City Beach or the Bahamas and Jimmy Buffet is sitting at the table next to you. Fantastic. You will need your GPS but it is well worth it. Great views of Old Hickory Lake! You honestly will feel like you are on vacation. On Wednesday night they had a great band there playing at 5:30 - some blues and a little rock and roll and beach tunes - don't ya know. The service is friendly and perfect! Our friends Tom and Donna Matthews dragged out again and we love this place. So how about the food? The Chicken Wings are 5 Stars! The best I think I have ever tasted. Lightly smoked with some spices and crushed Black Pepper - very different from what you are used to but the best. This is definitely "I need some now" kind of food. The Black-Eyed Pea Salsa is another home run. Joanne and I enjoyed a Sirloin Steak for 2 and it was a good solid steak and potato. We did not get to the oysters but I bet they are great. The beers on tap are solid - they had 5 from Bud Light to Yuengling, Amberbock and their own custom Black Pearl Ale (light summer ale). Salad Bar was fresh. Facilities are CLEAN y'all. Prices are moderate and more than satisfying for the ambience, product & service delivered. Yes we are going back there - lots - what a find!!! So put your shorts, loudest beach shirt and berks on and put this one on your list - often. We need a regulars Black Pearl Club meeting here - Arrrrh - Did I see the Black Pearl and Captain Morgan?
label: POS

text: Gracious Bakery & Cafe looks like it's the kind of business I love to support. Unfortunately my experience has been mixed. Gracious bills itself as a Cafe but this is a diservice as food (while tasty) is an afterthought. It is open for breakfast, but doesn't have a breakfast menu. You can only order whatever quiche or pastry may or may not be in the case. It is open for lunch but will not actually serve you from the lunch menu before 11:30... even if it's 11:10 and you're the only person in the shop and have driven across town for a sandwich. No sandwich assembly can occur before 11:30 sharp. A lack of concern for customer convenience was also an issue when placing a Thanksgiving order by phone. Whoever answered the phone wouldn't take the order, but said they would call back shortly. They never called. I've made several visits to Gracious. Some of the sandwiches, pastries and deserts I've had here have been very good but some were not. Gracious needs to develop consistency in the appeal of what they offer, and improve communication and effort to accommodate customers.
label: NEG

text: I have been driving by (and wanting to try) Pastiche for some time now. Last night, we made a last minute decision to drop on in for dinner and I am glad that we did. It wasn't very busy inside, and initial service was quick and efficient. Actually, this was a trend throughout the entire visit. I LOVE their wine list. For one, it's fairly large. Additionally, it is divided not only by type of wine but by price. I have always wondered why more restaurants don't do this! Needless to say, we ordered a pretty cheap, er, inexpensive bottle of Sauv Blanc (don't judge me!) and then turned our attention to food. For apps, I decided to try a cup of the mushroom soup and Pete ordered the sliders. The sliders come in three varieties -- burger, chicken salad, or pulled pork. On a whim, we asked if we could have one of each since coincidentally, an order consists of three. Both arrived at the table quickly and with an order of bread. The mushroom soup is oh-so-good. I have been craving a soup of its kind since The Warehouse in Colorado. Other restaurants seem to make it too creamy (yeah, there is such a thing) or with not enough 'shrooms for my liking. In my opinion, Pastiche hit the nail on the head with this soup. I'll most certainly be back for more! The sliders were equally yummy. The chicken salad was not traditional. It had an Indian flair with a pretty decent amount of curry. The burger had a delicious amount Gorgonzola on it and the pulled pork was also very good -- juicy with some thick, sweet BBQ sauce. For our main dishes, I ordered the bistro size of the chicken tacos and Pete had the duck a la orange. I was almost full by the time my taco arrived but it tasted so good that I downed it anyhow. Pete's dish came with beet risotto and spinach, all of which were very good. When we had finished we exclaimed that we couldn't possibly fit in any more food...that was, until our server casually slipped us some dessert menus and walked away. Have I even mentioned my sweet tooth? Well, it's alive and well. The dessert menu at Pastiche served as a sweet little devil on my shoulder : "Oh, come on. They have bistro portions of the brownie and ice cream! Chocolate ganache! Who are you to turn that down?" We decided that just mayyybe we could split something so we ordered a blueberry/vanilla/ginger pound cake with a blueberry compote and homemade vanilla bean ice cream. Oh my, was it ever amazing. We were practically using our forks as weapons for the last bite. I'm sure neighboring tables thought us weirdos. Great food, service, wine list and a fun time overall. For the month of June, I believe that Pastiche donates 5% of every bill to a charity of your choosing. What's not to love?

text: First of all, thank you fellow Yelpers for helping us find this place. It is Labor Day, and I have been watching a marathon of Anthony Bourdain's NO RESERVATIONS all day. After seeing Bourdain's trip to China, my fiance suggested Chinatown for dinner but added "something new," as Chinatown for us usually means David's Mah Lah Wah. I took to Yelp for some suggestions and after checking out a few reviews and menus, I stumbled upon Rangoon's very decent reviews and even more enticing menu. We figured it was time to be adventurous just like Mr. Bourdain, and try something than our standard Chinatown fare. Rangoon is on the verge of Chinatown, on 9th between Cherry and Arch street, down an unassuming street (unlike the brightly lit center of Chinatown) that you would not realize holds a Burmese gem. The dining room is very beautiful, neat and clean, more updated and sleek than some of your other Chinese restaurants. We ordered: chicken satay, thousand layer bread (with curry chicken sauce), and shared an entree of the Night Market Noodles. 1 - Chicken satay - ok, not a revelation but a decent dish with a nice peanut sauce. 2 - thousand layer bread - OH. EM. GEE. (forgive my use of the teenage girl vernacular to describe this dish but it is so fitting). JUST WOW. The bread is super thin and super crispy (an earlier Yelper that said similar to a big flat croissant is not far off) but for me it was all about the chicken curry broth. This may sound ridiculous but it was just so chicken-y! Huge pieces of chicken and potato make this more of a stew than a sauce but nevertheless, delicious. I wanted more. But we had an entree coming. 3 - Rangoon Night Market Noodle - once again, an absolute hit with both my fiance and myself. Perfectly cooked long egg noodles with a few scallions and pork, served with garlic oil and red onions on the side. Just enough of a kick in the oil and also loved that it was served on the side so you could dress the noodles to your whim. Sharing the entree meant we had plenty for a both of us with about a cup leftover for a snack later. Our waitress (whom I believe was one of the owners as well) was attentive and sweet; she asked us if it was a our first time as we were leaving and said next time we would have to try something different. We will definitely be back again but I don't think I could *not* have the thousand layer bread and night market noodles; they were just too good!

This restaurant seems to be a modern interpretation of meals enjoyed in this city for centuries. Richard, the maitre d', makes you feel like an old friend, even if it is your first time there. I have been welcomed to other places but it sometimes sounds like an afterthought. Richard greets each person and helps them feel like an honored guest. We decided to try Cookies & Dreams (Cookies and Cream), Strawberry Fields, The Bugsy (Carrot Cake), and The Ike Johnson (Red Velvet). The Bugsy cupcake was perfect. It had a flavorful and moist cake. The icing was smooth, not too sweet, and delicious. The Strawberry cake was moist, not too sweet, and filled with loads of strawberries. The icing was smooth, not too sweet, and topped with beautiful white pearl sprinkles. Another winner. The Red Velvet cake had such depth of flavor and was so moist. text: We went to Mosca's with some friends for a weeknight dinner. And that's the way to go, with friends you are willing to spend some time with. We started with a large bowl of the Italian crab salad. Like rest of the meal, it is served family style. So you wait your turn as the bowl makes its trip around the table and then help yourself to the salad. There was plenty of crab meat in the salad. The entrees were a large pan of their signature Oysters Mosca, a bowl of Chicken à la Grand, and a platter of Spaghetti with a Bordelaise sauce. All the dishes heavy with garlic. The family style presentation worked nicely. The only dish not served family style was the desserts, a piece of cheesecake & the Pineapple Fluff. Even so, everyone of us was given a spoon to taste the desserts as they circled around the table. What can I say that hasn't been repeated in many reviews? The meal was great. Service was all you would expect. Staff all helped each other keeping the water glasses full, the fresh hot bread coming, and making sure we had enough of what we wanted. Only one minor glitch, our first choice of wine was down to just one bottle. That wasn't going to be enough, so we went with our second choice. They have a nice bar and serve good cocktails.

It looked absolutely delicious when it arrived, but after my first bite, I was tempted to send it back. It was one of the chewiest cuts of steak i've ever had. The sauce was basically a thinner version of A-1 that completely overpowered the meat (that was absolutely flavorless anyways) The green beans it was served with were mushy, flavorless and sopping in oil. My boyfriend ordered the chopped steak with bleu cheese and sauteed onions, which we both thought was very good. Thankfully he shared it with me. The spinach side he ordered with it had no seasoning whatsoever, and was overloaded with raw garlic. All in all, the ambiance and service was good, but I would say that overall the culinary experience we were hoping for was non-existent. I did ask for my steak to be wrapped up so we could take it home and top a salad with it, because I cringed at the thought of letting a $41 steak just get thrown in the garbage. I hope that this is not considered one of Indianapolis's better places to get a steak.

My husband, who is less particular than me thought the stuffed crab shell and the shrimp with crab meat were inedible. He said the sushi at Whole Foods is substantially better than this, I didn't bother to try it. There were mixed reviews from the rest of the group; some people enjoyed it and have been repeat customers, others thought there wasn't enough selection, and others thought the food was just OK, many left hungry. The complaints about the texture of the meat led me to believe it was seitan rather than chicken with broccoli or pepper steak. The highlight of the buffet was the soft serve ice cream which was surprisingly creamy and delicious. The best part of the evening was being with family, so I suppose my $80 was well spent, but needless to say, I will not return to Ruby's.

I ordered a Bloody Mary, figuring it had to be top notch there and oh yes, it was. There was a hint of an usual spice in there (I'm thinking allspice) that didn't overpower it, but made it extra tasty. I believe they pickle their own green beans too, which may be the reason I was tasting the all spice. If the Bloody Mary is the most complex cocktail, then the bartenders at Maurepas are surely at Mensa level. The menu is divided into 2 sections grains, vegetables, and starch and then meat and fish. Note that several of the dishes may be in the first category but are not vegetarian, however, Danielle offered up suggestions and said they'd alter things to make them so. The soba noodles in hot broth (made from andouille, but you can get it made with veg-based broth) was just what I needed on this frigid day. It's served up with tofu on the side that might have been flash fried, not sure, but I liked what they did with it. The root vegetable gratin was thoroughly delectable, too. It took every ounce of control to not order one of the insanely amazing sounding desserts. Something to look forward to next time. I didn't want to, you know, "rush things." Oh screw it... It got busier as the evening went along, but the noise level stayed at a low "hum" due to the high ceilings and the peaceful sound of their water wall fountain. The food is amazing, and just as good as the original location in Ybor City. I was pleased to see that the menu is the same, and I knew that I'd be in for a terrific meal. I started with a seaweed salad that was served in a large martini glass over a bed of shredded carrot and turnip, and drizzled with sesame seed oil. Then I moved on to the Tempura Lobster Roll which is clearly the very best thing that I've ever eaten. I added the Spontaneous Combustion Roll which was a perfect blend of salmon, shrimp, initation crab, asparagus, avacado, scallions, and smelt roe, wrapped with grouper and then baked with spicy mayo. I'm not a huge fan of cream cheese, so I asked the chef not to include that in my roll, and he was more than accomodating. My friend ordered the Blue Moon Roll which has lump blue crab meat, asaparagus, and scallions with a teensy weensy bit of cream cheese. She also had the Tuna Summer of Love Roll which was spicy sesame tuna, mixed greens, scallions and smelt roe, and all wrapped up in rice paper. We left very full, very happy, and very sure that we'd be back again for more!

text: Taiwan Tea House was originally located the next plaza over (where Nordstrom Rack and Harry and Izzy's are now). Based on my own experience and others, it has been a terrible experience. Compared to King's Chef (I highly recommend. They have authentic food. It's got a great, dimmed light atmosphere. It's a place to go if you don't want buffet. Egg drop soup is the not the usual. It's less greasy and has more ingredients than MSG and eggs. If you ask for the Chinese menu, try the Five Spices Pork Ribs, Tropical Shrimp, Beef Tendons in clay Pot) Taiwan Tea House was overpriced and the food was too salty. The place is clean though. And the food isn't terrible though, especially if you must try some other Chinese food besides buffet. (I gave one star for this and for the quality of bubbles) Furthermore, what irked me the most was the service I received. The owner and his wife favor their customers. Depending on the ethnic background, they can be more welcoming. We don't get greeted and we have never been asked how our food tastes. (My family's dominant dialect is not mandarin) We've given them many chances to redeem their service, as I do not like to base observations on one occurrence. One time we ordered a mango smoothie with bubbles during our meal. They never gave it to us. After we reminded them, they gave it to us. But the smoothie had been sitting there forever and it was not fresh. They did not apologize. Another time, we had leftovers and asked if they not put all the foods together in one box bc the sauces and foods don't mix. It wasn't much work. But they disregarded it. Another time I asked to order a bubble drink to go, while I was eating a meal. They refused to give it to me that way because I'm sitting in the restaurant. I'm the kind of person that can never finish my entire drink at one sitting. And if I did not finish, I would have to waste it. So I forced myself to down it. Not the way I would like to enjoy my drink. I agree their quality of bubbles is the fairest in town. (Hence the one star) Sometimes their milk tea is watered down. It depends on the day. I would say 75% of the time, they ran out of bubbles. I would order their number 1 or 2 bubble drink on the menu, $3.75ea, and the owner would look at me blankly and say, "We don't have bubbles. It will take 45 min". 45 MINUTES? I know how to cook bubbles too (Buy it from Asia Mart at Castleton Area), if you cook a small amount, it'll take 10min. But the reason I want to come to their restaurant is bc I don't want to cook it myself at home. I never get an apology or "Do you want something else?" And if you read the three reviews before mine that have given it a low rating, they have also encountered problems with running out of bubbles. Also, I would enter their restaurant, go to the order area, and usually would not be acknowledged for about a couple of minutes. No "hi", or "Hold on a minute, I will be right with you." And at first, I thought it was a n "asian thing". But it's not. I've observed them with Americans in particular how they are friendly. As for other Asians, I've had Asian friends who felt the same way as I do. And they are Taiwanese or Mandarin-speaking. When Taiwan Tea House first opened, I was still in undergrad. I told many Asian students and many others found out about it on their own. I remember one Asian student in particular, sweet, nice girl (one you could never imagine to yell at someone in public), could not help but yell at the owner in his restaurant about his terrible service. My parents and family friends no longer go or recommend people to Taiwan Tea House for their biased services. Obviously since it's biased, there are many people who do not receive this same kind of service. Luckily, this may never happen to you. But I hope people are forewarned, and understand that there are a group of people that do feel this way. Although I miss those bubbles, I have not gone about 1.5 years now. Guess I better make it at home! :)
label: NEG

Dr. McCartney gave me the worse and best case scenarios and at least gave me some hope while helping me remain realistic. I went home with more meds and he suggested how to keep my cat hydrated while he was going through this kidney problem (he had stopped eating and drinking). He also gave me IV to take home in case I needed to do it myself. It was a long week but my cat got better. He was patient and attentive, despite how emotionally distraught I was. The other places were a little cold and didn't build rapport at all. They try their best to squeeze you in for a visit if you call at the last minute and its an emergency. The wait is always quick and they are efficient. The staff is always so friendly and they genuinely care about the animals they see. text: Food Tried: ($7 for three tacos) - Thai Chicken Taco - Sweet Taco - Spicy Taco First off, I owe one of my monumental, and quite common, apologies to Tacos Without Borders for not having written this review four weeks ago when I promised I would, but I ended up jumping on a plane to Paris and getting caught up in three weeks of work and now you know it's been a month and it's Christmas and the least I could do to finish getting caught up on what I said I would do before the end of the year. Also, what with having just switched phones, the photos on my old phone are now in Indianapolis, while I am in Denver for the holidays. Which basically means that I am doing the best I can and it's a sad effort and I apologize. So I had Tacos Without Borders back before Thanksgiving, and given that they can officially be titled The Most Elusive Food Truck in the city, when I found out that they would be parked outside one of the new breweries in town, Triton Brewing, I decided it was an unmissable opportunity: new food and new beer. When I came out, it was freezing, but as my food was prepared, I stood up in the front of the truck near the heater, and then brought my food into the brewery to enjoy it. I had the pleasure of trying a few Triton brews, and ended up pairing with the Magnificent Amber. I wanted to mention that because I made sure to mention to the bartender and various patrons that I was writing a blog and would definitely give props to Triton for putting me up while I sampled the fares. I can't remember exactly what I had, but I know that the base taco was a Thai chicken taco, and that the other two tacos I tried had the Thai sauce as a base, and one was curried, while the other was sweet. I couldn't honestly tell you which one I loved more, because they were all overwhelmingly flavorful in a great way, but the spicy, curried taco made my mouth burn so much that no beer nor water could abate the fire. Seriously, I have never had food so spice yet so amazingly good. I couldn't stop eating, despite the pain. I sacrificed myself for that meal, folks, and I'd do it again, despite what I'm sure was permanent tissue damage. Just warning folks: Tacos Without Borders does HOT. The presentation of my food was great: three tacos tucked in side-by-side, topped with fresh fruits and veggies, crunchy, hot, and juicy. The time I waited in the truck was well worth it, as was the price (as I could repeat again, which was standard for the trucks). For recommendations, it's been a while, but I feel like the best thing I could try to suggest is that there been better publicity for when you're going to be on the road, because often I've missed good opportunities to have great food from the truck because I couldn't plan ahead with advance notice.

Most normal humans would attempt to find a film by going to the appropriate "genre section" (Horror, Comedy, etc) and searching alphabetically by title. Although the organization of the store is bad, it pales in comparison to the worst part of the Casa Video experience: the late fees. THEY ARE PERFECTLY HAPPY TO MAKE YOU PAY A $100 LATE FEE FOR A VHS COPY OF MOVIE FROM 20 YEARS AGO. Comparing their late fees to say, Blockbuster's from back in the day yields a perfect mirror image of the stereotype of the kindly local shopkeeper and the heartless mega corporation. I have a friend who lost one of their films after a move. She attempted to pay to replace the movie; they ended up charging her almost $200. text: I went to the Crescent Pie & Sausage Company because they have a sharp website, the food looked good in the pictures and there's nothing like some hot pizza to nurse a hang over. The physical place was nice. It had a rustically-modern-industrialized-warehouse feel to it. Peach painted walls, austere wooden tables, a hard cement floor and large, clean windows that allow the Mid-city neighborhood on Banks street to be a real part of the ambiance here. The music selection was blue grass and folk. I definitely heard a fiddle in the mix. I liked the music. I went there for lunch on a Monday. I walk in and pick up a menu from a pile at the front door. The paper menus are glue-sticked to pieces of cardboard. Swear to God...true story. Strange. How very...very...rustic. I curl my lip and the give a little pout- mainly because mine has a brown food stain on it. The cute waiter recommends the Chicken Marcella Pizza. He said 'it was his favorite.' I agree to that and an order of house made dill potato chips. The food was much better than dog food but not quite as good as cat food. The chips were boring, brown, greasy, overcooked and burnt. I guess I've been pampered by Zapps for too long. They looked nice with chunks of sea salt and fresh dill sprinkled on top but those fresh flavors couldn't breathe on burnt palette. The pizza dough was very thin and dry. It seemed to be having an identity crises. It couldn't quite decide whether it was a cracker, a tortilla or some pita bread. The pizza was dressed with onions, chicken, mushrooms, a Marsala wine sauce, Parmesan and house made ricotta. The pizza was bland, but the ricotta was luscious. It would make one hell of an addition to some manicotti (if the right chef was standing behind the noodle.) I left uninspired but I'm a big advocate of second chances. I'm not quite done with this place. Their Mac and cheese has gotten some good reviews and maybe their sausage is amazing. But, as of right now, I left feeling pretty disappointed and bored with everything I ordered...except the diet coke. The diet coke was exceptional.

text: I just moved to New Orleans, and I know I really ought to be exploring more and trying all it has to offer...but I just can't stop going to Verti Marte. Trust the reviews and hit it up. Don't buy their overpriced groceries, though. EDIT: I hate to do this, but I gotta share my experiences with Yelp. I've repeatedly been charged more than the listed price for sandwiches. I wouldn't complain about paying $12 (!) for a shrimp po' boy if I knew that's what I was paying. But you order for one price off the menu, and get an entirely other price when you're checking out. I guess they've raised their prices (a lot) and neglected to update their menu. Leaving aside the fact that $12 is way too much for a sandwich from a deli (no matter how delicious), it's just in very, very poor taste to charge customers more than the listed price. I mean, c'mon. I've worked in the service industry and you don't do that. You just don't. Ever. The employees have been very nice about it and even hooked me up one time because they felt bad. And that deserves some good will. But I'm inclined to put up with the situation only so many times before I feel like going elsewhere, where I know I'm getting what I order. Verti Marte still gets three stars from me for unrivaled deliciousness, but I'm afraid they've lost me as a customer. A couple other notes of interest: Much of their meat is frozen. Delicious, but frozen. There are no prices on any of their beer or wine, making it extremely difficult to shop for. The guys working will be happy to give you the price of anything, of course, but it's frustrating when you're looking for a good budget red. Not to mention that their alcohol prices aren't the best. EDIT 2: Okay, they are still pulling this shit. And they're charging extra for cheese on sandwiches that come with cheese. And one of their employees is a total confrontational asshole. I swear I'd usually never write a review like this, but Verti Marte has legit broken my heart. Jerks.

She has my half of the money and the room is already paid for in full on her credit card and she has already called and given permission and is willing to give them whatever they need to allow me to stay there. This is apparently not sufficient as Einstein at the front desk tells me it needs to be on the Days Inn form. I explain the basics to him that she's not at home, it's 10pm, she's in her hotel room with no computer and no access to a fax machine. The hotel staff had confirmed their reservation and would make a note of the late arrival. Flash forward to 4:30am when my friends arrive, and they said they have no reservation for them and that the hotel is sold out. They did nothing for them. Total lack of professionalism, horrible reservation system, and total enforcement of absolutely stupid rules that make no sense. ZERO STARS! Days Inn, you suck so hard!...and not in the good way. text: I was in Indianapolis for work this past week and after a long day of reviewing files and interviews, I headed to my hotel exhausted and crashed. When I woke up I was starving and craving pizza. Of course, I turned to my trusty friend Yelp for some recommendations about places that delivered to my hotel and the only options that I got were chain options. Yuck! The only benefit of work travel is to be able to experience local cuisine and restaurants, but I was desperately in need of a pizza fix. So at 9 pm at night, I ventured into the cold dark streets of Indianapolis in hopeful search of pizza. About a mile from my hotel I saw a lit sign out of the corner of my eye proclaiming "Luca Pizza" So I pulled into the small strip mall, no there were no strippers there, and entered into what I can only describe as my momentary heaven. There were not many people in the restaurant and it looked like they were pretty much done for the night but the manager, maybe owner, asked how they could help and I expressed my great desire for a pizza. She told me all my options and I decided on their 14" pizza one-topping special. On a quick side note, I am not normally a fan of one topping pizza. It seems such a waste because part of the enjoyment is tasting the combination of all the extra flavors mixing with the tomato sauce and cheese. So at the very least I always want two toppings and generally those toppings are sausage and mushroom when I am not feeling overly particular, like this night. Well, fortune must have been smiling down on my because the manager/owner reminded me that the special was for one topping but that she was feeling generous and said if I wanted others she would add them for no additional charge. Their topping choices were pretty typical of most places and I was not feeling overly adventurous, so I chose sausage and mushroom. She told me it would take about 10 minutes to prepare and that I could have a seat. As I looked up, I saw her tossing the dough for my pizza. In a few moments she asked if I liked lots of mushrooms or less mushrooms on my pizza. It was nice getting a customized pie. About 15 minutes later she came out with an 18 inch pizza box explaining that she made the pizza a bit too big to fit in the 14" box. So instead, she put the pizza and the bread sticks that came with the special all into the 18" box. I paid, the total was under $20, and headed back to the hotel with a pipping hot pizza. When I got into the room I had to corral my three travelling penguins into the bathroom before I could open the pizza. Just a side note, I don't know about other people's travelling penguins but mine are really greedy bastards and will take all the food before I can even take a bite. So don't judge me for putting them in the bathroom, they like swimming in the tub while I eat and it is the only way I can have dinner in peace but I digress. So the pizza was good. It was quite cheesy and the sauce was very tasty. However, I was only able to eat about 3 slices before I began to feel full. So know that the pizza special can easily feed about 3 people. It was a good way to end a very long and tiring day and to get a taste of the locality.
label: POS

text: Cafe Luna has that beach shack appeal that almost makes me think it's a simple coffee shop, but it's more than that. I've hunkered down there in the daytime to get a little work done, ordered a panino and salad, sat by the fireplace in the sofas, and felt both productive (because of the work) and deliciously lazy (because it's a laid back beach town). There is wifi - to access it take your lappy up to the counter and they'll type in the password for you. Luna is also a proper sit down restaurant, especially for dinner service. It's so casual and small, it has the feeling more of being invited into a friend's home, or the quiet dinner of a B&B. Dinnertime is when I like to get a pizza, salad and dessert. Like the pizza with the egg on top - sometimes the egg is well done and I like it a little runny but it's still the one I prefer to order again. The individual pizzas might not initially look large, but it is substantial enough. And for dessert: tiramisu. It feeds two. Again, I enjoy ordering my food and flopping down with some friends at the sofa with the pile of goodies floating around the coffee table for everyone to graze at. It's just as easy to sit up in the regular chairs and dine properly, as most do. Most being relative - it's a small place with a handful of 2-tops. Overall, a quiet, simple escape from the buzz of bigger city restaurants. And it's Summerland, what's the rush?

text: One of my favorite casinos in all the land. I played poker professionally so I've had my fair share of casino visits, this Harrah's is probably one of my top 3 favorite casinos. I went to school in New Orleans for 4 years so had plenty of opportunities to visit here. I don't play table (or pit) games just poker. Their poker room isn't huge but I would say it probably has around 40 tables. It spreads 1/2 and 2/5 pretty regularly and both games are hilariously easy. I would say the skill heirarchy goes: LA, Northeast (Foxwoods/AC), Chicago, Vegas then New Orleans in overall skill level at these stakes. There can sometimes be a wait but it's well worth it. They use a TIME rake here which I actually like better, it makes stealing the blinds actually worth it, and you can get into some blind-on-blind action when it's folded around instead of having to chop. This is definitely a disadvantage to tighter players but poker is about adapting so if you can't do it that's on you. The ambiance and decor is top notch, they had just built their huge bar back when I was in school (spent something like a million dollars on just the bar itself iirc) and love how they have the go-go dancers in that room. One thing I will say is that for a regional casino it has the hottest women on staff compared to any other regionals. This place is a pretty good size too. I saw AC Slater (Mario Lopez) last time I was there. Their bathrooms to this day are the nicest of any casino I've been to including the Aria and Cosmo in Vegas. Overall if I'm back in town for some fun I will 100% be stopping in here at least once at some point in the evening. Nothing like beating up on a bunch of drunks at 3am at the poker tables. Oh and make sure you validate your parking at the poker host, they do it free if you play. And make sure you get a burger and cheese fries at Fuddruckers if it's still there. I used to stop in just for the fries..

text: Disappointing Takeout on Opening Day - My excitement to learn about a new Pho restaurant opening in the area (right around the corner from my house no less) quickly turned to disappointment after tasting the food that I ordered to-go on the restaurant's opening day. Normally, I would not patronize a restaurant until a few months after it has opened. I checked my IPhone for reviews before walking in and did not find any, except for the fact that this is a local chain, with other, already-established locations in Mt. Laurel and Cherry Hill/Voorhees. So I made my way inside to look at a menu and place my order. My first reaction was sticker shock at the prices, as compared to Pho Eden or Pho Garden in Cherry Hill. After getting the food I ordered, I was surprised at the prices even more, given the portion sizes and ingredients. The menu is fairly expansive, however, missing from it were vegetable spring rolls, or summer rolls with sliced cooked pork AND shrimp, which are typical in other Vietnamese restaurants (for the summer roll, the choice was either shrimp, chicken, or BBQ pork). I ordered one order of shrimp summer rolls ($4.50), and an order of Vermicelli with Grilled Chicken and vegetables for $8.00 and change, and waited only approx. 5-7 minutes for my order. The 2 summer rolls I received were large but underwhelming....5 or so shrimp in each with a large amount of shredded lettuce and only a few bits of basil in each (no beansprouts or carrot pieces). The Vermicelli chicken was also unsatisfying....a lot of overly-smoked/grilled chicken, with only a small amount of noodles, and the same shredded lettuce with a few bits of basil pile (no chopped peanuts, beansprouts, or chopped cucumber like at Pho Garden). I looked at the surroundings as I waited. There was another person waiting for takeout, and 2 or 3 patrons sitting in the dining portion. They were just as surprised to learn that the restaurant opened that day. (A good business practice would be to offer some sort of coupon or discount for patronizing the restaurant on the day it opened!). The interior is brand new and nice, but fairly dark, with inadequate air circulation (strong grilled smoke smell throughout). Maybe I will give this place another try again in a few months, trying something else on the menu. It is within walking distance of my house, and BYOB, so maybe sometime over the summer, when I can walk there. (There is also a brand-new Pinkberry-style frozen yogurt place a few doors down, for dessert). For now, I will stick to satisfying my Vietnamese cravings at Pho Garden (Kings Hwy) and Pho Eden (Springdale and Greentree) in Cherry Hill.

text: I buy stuff on line all the time. I made a huge mistake buying from this company without first checking their ratings, which are overwhelmingly bad. Goedekers quoted me a firm, fixed price for 3 appliances, and offered "free shipping" because the amount exceeded $999.00. After I paid the bill, they contacted me and said there would be a $138.00 shipping surcharge. I tried to protest the bait and switch technique with a supervisor, but got nowhere. He referred me to the fine print in a link on the company's Webpage. There, the fine print says there "may" be a shipping surcharge if you live in a rural area or a metropolitan area. (What's left?). Because the shipping surcharge apparently applies to all orders, the company's "free shipping" offer is a complete fraud on the consumer. Goedeker's apparent tactic is to lure consumers in by prominently offering "free shipping" on the main page of their website, only to later mousetrap the customer by invoking the disguised fine print once he or she commits to buy and pays for the merchandise. Since my initial conversation with Goedeker's "customer service" department, they have refused to return my calls or respond to my emails. I have not received the appliances. I did file a complaint with the on line Better Business Bureau, but that organization is reputed to be, and is, impotent. As I was told to expect, the BBB didn't do anything more than solicit a stock response from Goedekers and close out my complaint. However, I also filed a complaint with my state's Attorney General's Office. About a week ago, an investigator contacted me and took a report and got copies of my documentation (including screen shots of Goedeker's misleading website offers). I have asked the Attorney General to put a stop to Goedeker's "free shipping" bait and switch routine (which numerous consumers have complained about), and to bring suit against them or forbid them from doing business in my state if they won't cease and desist. I also filed a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission. A representative of that agency recently sent me a letter saying they, too, were investigating Goedeker's "free shipping" scam. I urge all other consumers who have been burned by this dishonest business practice to file similar complaints. If I don't receive my stuff, or at least a confirmation that it has been shipped, my next move will be to put the charge in dispute with my credit card company. If that fails, I intend to sue Goedekers. This company's conduct is really dishonest and reprehensible. Trust me and the many other consumers who have raged about this company on the Internet: You will regret it if you order from them or do business with them.

text: Cochon could possibly be New Orleans' answer to Chicago's Publican restaurant. The Publican has a special place in our hearts and while Cochon is no Publican, it felt like we were transported to New Orleans' take on gastronomy celebrating the pig, Cajun-style. Bread baskets can be undervalued sometimes since items on the menu are generally considered the star of the meal. But these rolls... soft to touch, warm on the inside, melting the whipped butter as I spread it, and slight sweetness on the taste. The crab-stuffed artichoke is beautifully served inside the "shell" of the artichoke leaves. Baked and topped with crispy bread crumbs, the taste of crab meat combined with the somewhat creamy dressing was well balanced. We also tried the fried alligators for the first time. The alligator meat bites were first deep fried until crispy and then tossed in chili garlic aioli. The entire dish had an oriental taste to it especially with the tangy hint coming from the aioli. The alligator meat itself was almost like a chewy form of chicken meat. My husband always teases me that I don't eat as much vegetables as him but after we finished our first plate of smothered greens, I asked to put in a second order of it. I loved it that much. The service was efficient and attentive although we were confused as to who our actual server was since two different servers stopped by our table periodically to see if everything was ok. Also, after the first server took our order, a second server came over to ask if we had ordered our food. No complains though as everything was efficient and well taken care of.

text: 5 STARS ALLLL THE WAY!!! The biggest reason I give this resort/hotel 5 stars is because Yelp wont let me give it 6. The Sandpearl was the most amazing place I have EVER stayed in. Walk into the lobby and the first thing you see is the amazing view out the back window overlooking the pool area, and just past that the Gulf. Also on the lobby level is Caretta's on the Gulf, the hotels restaurant. When I went to my room I was definitely impressed. Great size for a room. The decor is very modern and they have a great setup. The bathroom was unbelievable with a large sized tub and shower. Another nice feature is that every room on the resort has a balcony connected. Personally, my room overlooked Mandalay Ave so besides the bay in the distance nothing much to look at. However, my in-laws had a Gulf view room and WOW. I could sit on that balcony all day long. Another big plus is the beds, I don't know what kind of mattress it was but I do know it was definitely one of the most comfortable. The pool area is one of the best parts of the entire place. Nice sized pool to cool off in, two hot tubs. They also have poolside waiters who are always available. Not too pushy or in your face but they are there when you need them. The drinks are of course on the pricey side, just like everywhere else, but the Sandpearl does not hold back on the alcohol in their drinks. If your up to it, you can reserve a private cabana for the day for an extra price. Its a nice getaway from the hot Florida sun. Out on the beach they have a fire pit for guests to enjoy at night. Overall, I can't think of one thing that I did not enjoy about the hotel and would definitely recommend it to anyone staying in the area.

text: A little nostalgia upon seeing these street cars plying Tampa's street, being from San Francisco and all. Quite a history as well. Tampa's first electric streetcar line was way back in 1892, connecting Ybor City, Ballast Point, Hyde Park, Sulphur Springs and beyond. Unfortunately the line ceased to be in 1946 and it wasn't til 2002 that a 2.7 miles stretch of track came back into existence. They operate three distinct cars, the Breezer, which is open-aired, much like the trollies in S.F., the Standard and the Birney. Now, the Birney was saved from a Sulphur Springs backyard and lovingly restored through 10,000 volunteer hours. It's a replica of the ones that were operated in Tampa from 1920's-1946 and boasts cherry seats, oak frames and mahogany. A nice way to tool through neighborhoods and not too expensive. Hope more lines will sring up here in Pinellas County.

text: Barone's has all the right ingredients for the possibility of a successful office party. The restaurant is divided into several separate spaces, so we were able to get crazy with our annual re-gifting game without annoying the rest of the diners. The pasta dishes were delicious. They accommodated requests for gift and wine tables to be set up before we arrived. Unfortunately, there were far more cons than pros. Barone's seriously lacks organization and professionalism for large group planning. When I called to ask about pricing packages, I was told that tax would be waived if we paid in cash. This meant that the total cost per person fell within my budget goal, and so I went ahead and made a reservation. A couple weeks later, when I stopped in to choose the menu, I was told that the person I spoke with on the phone was misinformed, and that we would be charged 5% tax rather than 7%. Since this would raise the cost per person by a dollar, and I was not going to go around asking everyone who had already RSVP'd to give me another dollar, I had to go back the next day to speak with a manager. I explained my concerns to the manager, hoping that he'd lower the cost of the dinner so that the 5% increase in price wouldn't change my total cost per person. My main concern was that since my total cost included a tip, the restaurant would take what they were owed, but the servers wouldn't receive their 20% cut. The manager assured me that it would not be an issue because HE would be the server the evening of our event, and since he understood the situation, he just wouldn't take tip. "Seriously, don't worry about it," I was assured. So the night of the party came, and there were several red flags from the start. First, the manager was nowhere to be seen. It would have been nice to be greeted by someone who was familiar with all of my requests upon arrival, perhaps a review of the menu that had been chosen. But when I got there, the hostess simply pointed me in the direction of the back room and I was on my own. Said room happened to be freezing. I mentioned it to a worker, and was told that the heat was just turned on for that room. The room never warmed to a comfortable temperature, and I actually had a few diners who ate their entire dinners with their winter coats on. The bathroom that was at the back of our room was gross. It looked like someone had given himself a haircut in there before we arrived, little snips of hair all over the sink, and a canister of hair pomade on the counter. A friend had to wipe up the sink before the rest of the party arrived. There were also no paper towels and the room was running low on toilet paper. It took several requests before these changes were made. The service itself was good. From what I experienced at my own table, drinks and food arrived in a timely manner, and the servers were friendly. Aside from the pasta course, no one really seemed impressed by their food. Portions were huge, but taste was forgettable. The manager finally showed up about halfway through our dinner to ask how we wanted our dessert served, cut up all the cakes for us, and then disappeared again. More issues, or maybe the same issue, arrived when it was time to pay. We were charged for an extra diner; I mistakenly said that we had 31, and that is how many the manager put on our bill, despite the fact that I know he MUST have counted how many plates went out so that he'd be able to tally up our dues later on. He had to know I had miscounted. Oh, and hey, remember when I was told that gratuity would NOT be included and that the manager would be our server so we shouldn't worry about an inadequate tip? Yeah, well gratuity WAS included, and we had not collected enough money to meet the total. I had to ask the poor server (who was NOT the manager) to remove the gratuity from the check so that we could afford the bill, and then I ended up throwing in some extra cash that I (luckily, and uncharacteristically) had in my wallet to come closer to what the total should have been with a 20% tip. *MAJOR GUILT* The manager made an appearance again as we were on our way out, and we pointed to a large bottle of wine that had been opened but not otherwise touched, offering it to him and his servers. "Ugh, I don't drink wine. That stuff is like grape juice," he scoffed, as his cell phone rang with some trancey club beats. Sorry playa. I'll leave you to your Red Bull and vodka and fist pump my way out the door. And my coworkers and I will NOT be back for next year's winter soiree.

text: Had take out here and I always get the same thing - Duck Confit Salad. First, call to make sure they are open. Once, I tried to do take out and they were closed for a private reception. The Duck Confit is usually a whole leg that just breaks by the touch of your knife. They give you more Duck than salad. Note: this is a rather light dish so I suggest you order something else. text: This is the second Iron Hill I have been to, the other in W. Chester. I believe the original. My boyfriend, son and I went on a random Tuesday night, we got a table right away at round 530, but by the time we left, around 730, I believe there was a wait. ANYWAY, we didn't wait long for a delightful server to greet us. She was knowledgeable about the beers, from which we started with the sampler (a stupid thing to order because any sample is free and you can taste all of them!) The beers are good. We then just ordered a couple aps. VERY VERY fair. The hummus plate was beyond boring. Do not advertise that the hummus plate comes with cucumber, when they are diced and clearly preped for salads. SLICED cucumbers for dipping is what hummus calls for. The kids menu is great. There is a ton to choose from, and keeping food coming for little ones is a must! Like I said, by the end of our meal, it was getting tight. The dining area (not bar area) has maybe two to many tables (the free standing ones) in it. A lot of me moving my chair in and out to allow for rushed servers to squeeze by. Also, like I said, our server was great, however, a couple tables away I noticed a different server a bit too casual. He was leaning on and all around his table. I believe at one point he had his foot up on a empty chair. Patrons come to a restaurant to be served. Most of us are normal, hard working ppl and for maybe two hours are able to sneak out to a nice dinner maybe once or twice a month. We are spending our hard earned money to pay for food, drinks, service and tip, PLEASE treat us accordingly. It's a treat to go out, please serve me, and of course be casual, but ultimately our job IS to serve outstandingly, not flop all over my table, come on. All in all tho, the restaurant had charm, it just wasn't over-whelming like I maybe expected a new restaurant to have. It seems good to go with a couple buddies and have some beers, I'd go back.

text: I am thrilled to have a nice new Japanese restaurant so close to home! What makes this place special is they appreciate your business and go out of their way to make you feel special! They want to get to know their customers! It has only been open for a week or so and it had a nice crowd on a Saturday night. The restaurant is cozy, trendy and nicely decorated with linen table cloths. It even has small private rooms for a small party and also a sushi bar. You forget you are in a small strip mall. The 4 of us all tried different dishes. I started with the miso soup ($5)...I always judge a good Japanese restaurant by the miso soup and this was delicious! The right temperature too! My main dish was the Sushi/sashimi combo ($25.) and the fish was succulent, fresh and melted in my mouth like good sushi should be. It was quality! There were 4 of us and we tried each others dishes. The calamari salad ($13) was fresh as could be with a light batter on the calamari. The best appetizer was the Rock Shrimp Tempura ($12) sweet and spicy and wow...delish! The salmon Teriyaki was excellent! ($18)...it came with fresh veggies an they were done perfectly! The filet Mignon steak ($28) was cooked exactly the way it was asked for! Nice flavor and generous portion. The chicken teriyaki looked like a generous portion ($16)...even had left overs to take home on that dish. Service was over the top great! This tends to be a bit pricey and miso soup or salad is not included in the traditional combo meals, but it is more upscale than most Japanese restaurants and the quality shows! I almost forgot to mention, the chopsticks are not the wooden ones that splinter...they are translucent and quite cool! In fact all of the dishes are trendy and make a nice presentation! Don't forget to BYOB! They will even supply a nice wine bucket for keeping it cold. We were informed the menu will have even more to choose from in July or August. I look forward to trying the Pad Thai as that will be on their new menu! Anyway... Does it get any better? Good service...good food and a bottle of red!!!

Since that time I have enjoyed quite a few items off the menu, and to my delight each one is as good as the last. As a critique - the portions are huge - to big for me, and I am a big guy - I work out, am in good shape, and weigh 220 - so, if you have an "endless pit teen" or you are one of those people that loves the hearty portions - this is a great place for you. Also, the servings are a little much for me - like the sour cream and guacamole... They were both offered in HUGE portions on my plate, and were kind of overwhelming... Overall - I would suggest going here - enjoy a breakfast combo plate, or a burro - you won't be disappointed, and most of all you will have a great experience with a friendly staff that is ready to serve... text: Too many fair trade stores use the "fair trade" label to get away with selling overpriced or low quality merchandise, banking on those people who will buy anything as long as it saves a rainforest. Plowsharing Crafts is definitely NOT that kind of store. They have a wonderful selection of products at surprisingly low prices. I was particularly impressed by the jewelry, which covered everything from delicate paper rings to hefty silver necklaces. I picked up an adorable pair of beaded hoop earrings that literally made me stop and stare as I was leaving the store. They also have a nice selection of ceramics and other housewares, as well as handmade books and picture frames. As someone who really, really can't pull of the cute hippy look I was pleased that a good portion of their clothing is more traditional, everyday stuff (though there are plenty of long flowy dresses and peasant tops if that's your thing). The staff were delightful, probably helped by the fact that they're all volunteers. I had a great chat with one of them about some of the wall tapestries. Plowshare is my new first stop when I need to buy gifts for friends and family. If you're looking to buy some gifts or decorate your home or just want to browse through some beautiful, creative products, check it out.

text: Damn right, I spent my birthday gettin' down at Puckett's! Homestyle. After the yelp elite event at Puckett's months ago, I couldn't wash the flavor of their ribs out of my desire palate nor quench it with something else. Hence, when the old birthday rolled around and my hubs asked where I would like to dine it was an obvious choice for me. Puckett's, 100%. We set up the reservation online (like a lazy yelper) and scooted through the crowd of folks drooling by the door as they watched other diners receive their meals. Always a sign of a good place: 1. A wait and 2. ability to make reservation so that you don't have to. So we get to the table and the ambiance is truly completed as a no-name one-man-band steps up on the Puckett's stage to croon and pick (and pass around his duct tape tip bucket...I'm not judging!). For an app, we ordered the sweet potato fries which came crispy and that is about all I can remember after I inhaled them. Sooner than expected my full slab of birthday ribs made an entrance but were placed in front of my husband. After a quick," Those belong to me," with a cheerful smile and a laugh out of the server the plates were swapped and my napkin was tucked in my shirt just as fast as you can blink. Savory, smokey and spiced perfectly-the ribs were heavenly. Within minutes I was down to half a slab. I am a girl that can eat! The other half actually made it home for another meal although our server did ask whether we needed wipes and forks for the ride home. Profiling much? All in all it was fantastic night and for $48.00 for two, I can't complain. Awesome food. I just can't get over it!

text: I just got back from my first visit to the brand new Walmart Supercenter here in town. Finally, the North Valleys have a Walmart! What's more, the North Valleys finally have a major shopping presence. The opening was this morning and it was a very festive occasion with a pretty decent turnout from the locals. The store is beautiful and the location around it is visually striking. There was an abundance of employees and suits on hand to welcome the shoppers and ask if any assistance was needed. The store is clean and organized, as is expected from a brand new store. The layout is a bit different from the other stores in town that I'm accustomed to shopping at. It's going to be a while before I become fully comfortable with it and know where to find the paper towels automatically. The grocery section is well stocked with the usual suspects however, I did notice that the coffee creamer selection was pretty limited compared to the other Walmarts in town. Nothing major but it definitely registered on my radar. It made me wonder what other selections might be limited. Time will tell when I do my first major grocery shopping trip there later this month. The employees seemed very friendly, of course, I'm sure a lot of that was due to it being opening day. But on the whole, I would say they were as excited as the shoppers. It made for a very fun atmosphere to shop in, though I did get a little tired of being asked how they could help me by about the 10th time. The food vendor this particular location is Subway sandwiches which was neither a foregone conclusion nor a surprise. We already have two Subways up here and two McDonald's so either vendor would have been rather superfluous. I wish they could have found a different vendor to work with, even though I know Walmart tends to default to Subway or McDonald's these days. Some variety would have been nice. It'd also be nice if they had some place to get a hot cup of coffee. I sure would have liked it this morning. Maybe Subway serves coffee, if so I didn't see any obvious signs to that effect. The biggest mark against this location is the utter lack of self-checkout lanes. There are NONE to be found. Each side of the store has some "speedy" checkout lines (none of which were at all speedy when it came time to check out, by the way), but the lace of self-checkout is a major problem. That disappointed me more than anything else. There's some room for improvement here, to be sure, but I think on the whole it's a great store. The parking lot is laid out thoughtfully and is easy to navigate, the store looks great inside and out and the experience is rather pleasant. I'm sure my review will change as time goes on but I wanted to get this out there!
label: POS

text: From folklore to Bangalore, even Vishnu, who would have to aggressively flail every arm on his body to get service here, would frown on such epic indifference. Was the food good? Yes. In the latter case, I think they try, but can't quite nail it. In the former, they could nail it, but don't try. Honestly, I was never really even spoken to at at Flavor of India. Upon entering, I stood in the foyer for a couple minutes before being acknowledged from afar with a shout of "Just a minute, sir." A booth was hurriedly set, and I was waved in from across the restaurant. Upon my triumphant land grab, I beamingly waited for the dulcet tones of a drink order request . . . and waited . . . . . . and waited. Finally, I tired of waiting and sauntered off to the buffet. "Excuse me," I pleaded, "I'd like another beer, please," as I chucked the check to the other side of the table. Put yer dirty tines on the table top, oh so recently swabbed with dirty club soda and smeared with swimming bacteria. Sheesh. Is it that hard and costly to just bring a clean fork? text: I hope I can update this review soon with better news, burrito lovers. I thought the haters who complained about the odd hours, unexplained closings, weird menu strategies and so forth were just less interested in a great burrito than I was. I love a great burrito, and will put up with a lot to get it! However, my most recent experience last week was just depressing. I was hoping for my old standby, a black bean burrito with plantains and guacamole. No more plain old black bean burrito on the menu, so I had to get a combination. No problem! Guacamole burrito it is. I even remember to say "to stay" before ordering to forestall that inevitable question. I get the bathroom key (locked to prevent non-paying customers from using it -- sort of understandable!) and read the proliferating signs about the salsa limits (take only a few! that means 2!). So far, only slightly annoying. Now, I knew we probably wouldn't be in for homemade tortillas. I've lived through several flip-flops in this policy -- once it was explained to me near the beginning of the school year that there are "too many customers" so they had to stop using homemade tortillas. Ok. No matter. But the burrito I got was nothing short of a travesty. Put together lumpily so that I started out with three or four bites of straight up rice, this was my first UN-toasted MexiCali burrito. Why oh why? The toasting was the best part! The cheese was cold, I tell you. Cold. Worst, the salsas were strange and watery -- the hot salsa's one attribute was wetness. I guess even with the strict two-salsa-per-customer limit the price of tomatoes and peppers is too high to make them taste like anything? I can't say I won't be back, because MexiCali is like that dreadful friend who nonetheless is incredibly fun two or three times a year. But I do wonder how in the world this place survives with such an attitude: The Customer Is A Major Inconvenience.

Each a flat bread and one got the "octopus" salad. The flat bread was ok, but I have to put quotes around since there was hardly any octopus in the salad. Next came the entrees. The seafood saffron stew came with a hefty pricetag, but not much else to it. Not sure why you would serve a saffron broth and no bread either. It was just different shell fish in a small bowl. The pork chop was good and maybe the favorite of the evening. The Steak Frites were ok and the Tuna was small in portion and not terribly exciting. The total came to $50 a person. Again, I would easily pay more than that if I felt it was worth it, but it isn't at the Saint James. Everything was under seasoned and small portioned. When we got back to our house, the fellas ordered a pizza. And yes, it is loud since there is nothing but hard surfaces. From what I could tell, it doesn't matter. This was clearly the place to be. text: Another reviewer who called this gem "hidden in plain sight" was right on the money. You never eat in Times Square if you want good food in New York, right? So how is it possible to find such an un-freaking-believable dinner spot around the corner from Bourbon Street in New Orleans?? Manfriend and I took a ten-day road trip from Denver to Washington DC and stopped at many places in the south. The meal we had at Louisiana Bistro topped every other meal of the trip. We walked in around 9:30pm and were lucky to get seated immediately even though you usually need reservations (it's very small). We started with the Fried Green Tomatoes and the Crab Cakes, both bursting with spicy flavor. The sweet corn maque choux on the crab cake was unlike anything I'd ever eaten before, sweet and spicy with an interesting texture. I'm not a big jalapeno person, but the jalapeno hollandaise on the friend green tomatoes was wonderful. For our entrees I had the crab and asparagus (again, the textures of this dish were as interesting and complementary as the flavors...crunchiness, softness, smoothness, tangyness, saltiness, sweetness...it's pretty much a party in your mouth). My boyfriend got a seafood etoufee that was super shrimpy/crawfishy and covered in delicious red sauce (red sauce is the technical term for whatever that tomato-based soupy jambalaya liquid is, right?). The topper was the cream cheese ice cream covered in strawberries and a balsamic glaze. Weird and wonderful. I wanted to take this chef with me on all my future travels. If you are in New Orleans, save some of your cash for booze and spend it here instead. You won't be disappointed.
