text: I had the most baffling customer service experience here in my life. It was mostly terrible and insulting, but it was so uncalled for that mostly it left me feeling sort of confused and amused. My bf and i were visiting NOLA and happened upon this store while out exploring. We saw a statue of a Baphomet that we *loved* but the lady behind the counter seemed like she was being held there against her will, rather than working as paid employee in a tourist district. No greeting, no 'can i help you?', no friendly chat... my bf asked her 'how's it going' and she glanced at him and took a moment before replying 'fine.' and looking away again. We decided to come back later and talk to a happier member of staff. On our last day we came in, and lo and behold, the same woman is there. She was in a room behind the front counter, loudly ranting about something to someone in the back room that we couldn't see. She paid us no mind as we browsed around, and eventually we stopped in front of the statue and tried to make eye contact with her. We were only about 7 feet away and in plain view, but she just kept on ranting and ignoring us. I decided to just bring the statue to the front counter so we could maybe get some service. The moment i touched the statue, she stormed out, grabbed it from me and said to us 'don't touch that! I don't know WHY people are always touching things. You're going to break it.' I was rather taken aback and annoyed, especially as there were no 'do not touch' signs anywhere, so i replied in a slightly terse voice 'sorry, we waiting for some customer service.' She angrily replied 'this isn't customer service, it's witchcraft! If you want something you just have to say 'hey you, i want this fucking thing!' Now, first off, for someone with signs all over the store saying 'don't steal, it's bad karma' you'd think their belief in this would extend to treating people nicely. Secondly, i used to work in a store that sold witchcraft stuff, and half the things she was selling were things i was selling 10 years ago in a store in Canada. It's not witchcraft, it's retail. She said she would go to the back and get us a statue in a box, and we told her not to worry, we didn't want it anymore. After all, if she has more in a box, clearly it's something we could find elsewhere (which we did, for nearly 70 dollars cheaper!) As we left, she yelled 'good! I'm in no mood for sensitive people today' so my boyfriend looked over his should and softly said 'YOU'RE sensitive.' After that, she yelled a few more obscenities at our backs as we walked out. Outside the shop, a man and a woman were sitting on a bench, and the woman said 'oh no, sorry, she's in one of her moods. They renamed the street she lives on so she's pretty upset. I'm a friend of hers and help out around here, so if you want, i can help you guys?' We said it was alright and thanked her, and as we were speaking, the cranky-pants store lady stormed out, pointing at us and telling us to get the hell out of her store. Her friend tried to reason with her, saying 'now, you're just in a bad mood, these people seem nice and polite' but she replied that she never wanted to see us ever again. It was just WEIRD since she was SO upset. Like, yelling, pointing, cussing upset... I know there are two sides to every story, but i swear on my mother's life that my bf and i acted exactly as i described and live up to the Canadian stereotype of being polite and pleasant. Hher hostility seemed INCREDIBLY unwarranted and very surprising. About 30 minutes later, we ran into a man who had been sitting on the bench who explained to us that he was new to the city and that his friends were friends with her. They had all warned him to watch out because (and i quote) she is the biggest bitch in New Orleans. According to him, she was still ranting about us when he left the store 20 minutes later. Seriously?! My boyfriend and i laugh about the experience now, and we've made sure to tell our friends that if they ever go to NOLA, they have to go to Esoterica and try to pick up the Baphomet statue haha!

I don't know if they're trying to stay a secret - but they sure are succeeding! Finally one day my colleagues and I decided to try it out for lunch. Walking in, it is such an odd place - primarily because its trying to use the same space and layout for both a lunch restaurant and a late night bar/dance floor/music venue. The restaurant was eerily quiet - and the few tables they have are spaced so far apart you really don't know where to sit. There were 2 other tables seated at the time, but both were halfway across the place from the nearest open table. We ended up sitting at a high top in the middle of the dance floor - definitely not 'cozy'. Our server was friendly, but wasn't around very often. I think he was both serving food, and bartending - and there is a good chance he might of been at least helping cook the food as well. The menu looked good - it just took forever to order and even longer to get our food. After the strange ambiance and poor service, we did not expect much from our meal. However - the food was shockingly good! I wish I could give separate ratings for the food vs. the service and ambiance. Once the food actually came, my pork sliders were fantastic! My colleagues had some burgers - all delicious and cooked to the proper temperature. We all left pleasantly surprised at the food. Overall the food is worth it, but only if you've got a long lunch break and thick skin for bad service. I'll probably be back, but only if I'm not in a rush.

text: I love to go shopping at the Co-op...when I can afford it! Having been a vegetarian for 14 years, I certainly learned to appreciate the foods that most people find gross or unpleasant like tempeh, tofu, seaweed, and wheat grass. If you're a weirdo like me in that case, you'll love this store for its wide selection of both local and more commercial organic and healthy-type foods. This was the only place in Tucson that I was able to get my favorite kind of soy jerkey for years. Sometimes, Id grab one of their Tempeh BLT's from their deli fridge for a quick lunch (theres loads of great stuff in there!). And although I rarely bought any, their fresh daily made soups are pretty darn good. I love the fact that you can buy LOCAL, Organic produce here. Ive had a few opportunities to discuss with the man in charge there and firstly, its important to know that they pay fair rates for local produce. Its good to know that the people putting in the hard work for the crop are getting paid good money for it. They dont take a huge cut for themselves, and prices wind up being reasonable considering you can call the farmer yourself (or just ask an employee there) about what nutrients and fertilizers were used in the making of your food. I just love the idea of helping out the little guy, too. So much so that I have heavily considered becoming a specialty organic tomato supplier for them in the past! Who knows? Maybe some day I will! I sure wont be able to eat ALL those san marzanos and black heirlooms by myself. Last thing I go here for when I really plan on treating myself is loose leaf tea. This is one of the best tea selections Ive ever seen, and anyone who enjoys the stuff in its true form rather than those crappy little bagged things will really be appreciative of the Co-op. I wish their prices for some items were lower, but the quality you get with most of their stuff is just so far any beyond anywhere else, it makes it worth the price. Love it, will return as frequently as my wallet will allow.

text: At first glance, Tapestry looks like a pretentious high-end bar where the hipsters and yuppies hang out. Beer selection is substantial and impressive, and so is their draft list. Drink and food specials are written down at the chalkboards posted in the back of the large room, but don't miss out on the amazing cocktail list (Planter's Punch with Kraken rum? YES!). Bonus points for cute bartenders at the front, mmhm. Food prices here are reasonable with entrees starting at $10 -- and they don't skip on the portion sizes. They also have a pretty nifty build-your-burger menu -- start with beef or turkey, lettuce tomato and/or onion, then add on additional toppings for 50 cents to a dollar apiece. My burger was perfectly cooked to order with yum bacon, and would've been perfect had it not been for the substantially thick slice of cheddar. Other than that, the burger and fries were delicious and I appreciated the side garlic aioli. A girlfriend and I had a mix up with our orders which the friendly staff were more than apologetic for, but the new plates took awhile to return to the table. Blaming it on the fact that it was a busy hour, though... at least for now. Our server was also great about our birthday cake, keeping it chilled in the kitchen and then serving it lit with candles at the right time (and thankfully, no singing!). As always, parking around South St is a pain... be patient and traverse the streets carefully.

The receptionist is very friendly, which is actually true of everyone that I've ever interacted with there. The massage rooms are actually on the larger side and of course, each has the relaxing music playing in the background. What I've always found interesting is that just about every time I go, I often see more men than women, although I'm told the clientele is about 50/50. As a guy, I like coming here as the place is not all foo-foo like so many spas can be. I've been coming here for about 4 months now and always request the same therapist and she does wonders on my back. I've never had any difficulty in scheduling appointments that are convenient for me. Someone will always call you the night before to remind you of your appointment. If you join their email list, you'll be notified of their monthly specials. They offer a variety of massages and prices are actually reasonable. I really look forward to my monthly massages! The only downside is parking can be a challenge at times. They have a decent size circular driveway, but at busy times, it's just simply not enough space. Sometimes cars can be parked in such a way that it makes it a bit difficult to get out of there. But it's certainly not bad enough to keep me away!

text: The town of Phoenixville, PA definitely is like a phoenix rising from the ashes. The towns' main street (Bridge St.) is wonderful. Daddy Mims is nicely decorated, clean, and friendly. When a restaurant charges $100+ for dinner (2 people) you should expect perfection. Daddy Mims got the French Bistro part of SUPER SMALL portion sizes to a tee. First Course: Creole Seafood Gumbo - The soup was flavorful but barely coated the bottom of the large soup bowl (maybe 4 oz.). The crab meat was all broken up from stirring the pot. Where is the andouille and okra? Second Course: Commander Palace style shrimp remoulade - There were two large shrimp (yes two !!!) on the plate with a nicely spiced remoulade sauce and garnish. Taste was good what there was of it. Shrimp cocktail usually comes with six shrimp. Do you think they could at least serve four shrimp? Third Course: Shrimp etouffee served over jambalaya and Cajun style roast pork shoulder with smoked bacon over mashed sweet potatoes - Once again, two large shrimp on about 1 cup of jambalaya. The jambalaya was flavorful but unremarkable. I make better jambalaya as does Zatarains. Next to the jambalaya was about 1 cup of mashed sweet potatoes with a small amount (maybe 1 oz.) of pulled pork shoulder strings. The sweet potatoes were excellent. Fourth Course: White Chocolate Bread Pudding with whiskey sauce - This desert is to die for. I can not say enough about how GOOD this was. Go to Daddy Mims just for this desert. Skip the rest of the Taste of New Orleans. Yum !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Beverage: Unsweetened Iced Tea - The tea was weak. The tea bag was waved across the water. Sweetening options limited to sugar and Equal. Luzerne Tea is available in this part of the country. Luzerne is a southern robust tea not like a woossie Tetley. The service was very good to excellent. On a Sunday evening there were four two-top tables (besides us) and a party of six table being served. Maybe the crowds are getting the feed bag on somewhere else before coming to get the bread pudding desert later. Rating (max 4 stars): Overall - 2 stars. Value - 0.5 star. Food - 1.5 stars. Service - 3 stars. Atmosphere - 2.5 stars. Finally, I will never pay $40.00 for the Tour of New Orleans again due mainly to the portion sizes. If it were not for the desert this meal would have been a total rip-off. Americans want a good meal, large belly busting portions and low low prices. We are NOT the French !!!!!!!!!!!!

text: Okura is the best sushi restaurant this side of Kyoto. They serve high quality fish, interesting and unique (but not weird) roll combinations, and you can't beat the prices. Kailon, the owner + sushi chef, is super friendly. Expect to strike up a convo if you sit at the sushi bar. I highly recommend the Hamachio carpaccio appetizer (thinly sliced yellowtail sitting in a bath of slightly spicy chili oil, with scallions, eel sauce and crunchy little roe on top), and the W.W. Roll. Don't ask me what's in this 2nd one, but it's tempura fried, covered in crab strips, and tastes like sushi heaven. The spicy tuna with cucumber wrap (instead of rice) is also worth a try -- the texture/temperature contrast is addictive. I've been to the fancy shmancy joints in NYC and Philly, and will continue to go for special occasions or a change of pace, but when my gut is aching for some broiled eel or tempura'd shrimp, Okura's where you'll find me.

text: This review pertains mainly to the Indian Garden's dinner hours: The Indian Garden may have the same name as any other Indian restaurant you've been to, but it certainly sets itself apart with its quality food and service. You can choose from a variety of meats, sauces, rices, breads, and veggies that all combine splendidly, no matter the selection. Rest assured, the meats will be cooked perfectly, the sauces will be rich and flavorful, the nan will be warm and soft, and the vegetables will be zestful. You can tell that everything (at least the food) is authentically cooked and it's not even outlandishly priced. And if you don't feel like eating out, the take-out is just as good. For the most part, the Garden's lunch buffet beats the local competition. The selection and freshness of the food obviously don't compare to any entree's quality, but if you're looking for a quick and filling bite of Indian food, this is your place. In terms of service, the servers are all very friendly and you can tell that they love their business and value their customers. My family has been going to this restaurant (although it has moved several times) for years and it has never disappointed. In fact, when I was a kid, the owner used to give me a free mango lassi, so if you have a cute little girl, be sure to expect one on the house. My favorites: - mango pudding - tandori chicken tikki - fish tikki masala (salmon..mmm...) - crab meat curry - chicken korma - naan & garlic naan - chicken tikki marsala

text: JC Dobbs is back!! One of the premiere live music venues that features live local bands and musicians has been resurrected. Grendal's lair was an even bigger live music and concert venue than Dobbs and once it shutdown, all the funky spots on the 'HIPPEST STREET AROUND" started falling like domino's. It was so sad to all who enjoyed live music every night, not just on weekends. Dobbs was a funky little bar that had a restaurant and game room upstairs and you had to walk past the band that was performing onstage to get there. When I walked past the band playing and went up the stairs, at one point you were directly behind the band on the same level and you felt like you were on the stage with them as a member. You could expect to hear any kind of music on any night and sometimes I saw a few well know musicians like Cyndi Lauper, Robert Plant, Jackson Browne, Living Colour, George Clinton and more jamming away to our surprise and pleasure. There was a big Irish guy named Shamus who always let me in thru the musicians entrance so I wouldn't have to pay a cover charge and then the fun began! I went to the new JC Dobbs the other night to see an old friend, Mike Tyler perform there and the spot looked great, and they even sell food upstairs and I'm told it's good and I had a great time. It made me remember the groups like Johnny O and the Classic Dogs of Love, Strawberry Affair, PM & the New Breed, Mike Tyler & Montana, Doug Grisby & Candi, Chuck Treese, Starr Cullars & Lindsay. Oh, and did I mention the great service...one of the group asked the waitress if they had a mojito, and the waitress said, yes, that 's our 'dragon' (something or other) drink. Not only do I get to reap the frenzied book collector benefits, but I get to rest easy at night knowing I am supporting my local library! Inside of the library proper, you have the reception desk to the right - always staffed with obvious hard workers - and the glass-enclosed young readers' room. The far right wall is comprised of a Genealogy room, group study room, and computer lab. The rest of the library is shelves and computers, very clearly marked and easily navigable. If you cannot find what you're looking for, simply log on to the HCPLC catalog and request your item from any library in the Hillsborough County Cooperative and have it shipped to this branch for pickup, free of charge! I love you, library. ~the tune to 'Reading Rainbow' plays faintly overhead~

text: Re: other fussy elitist reviewers - one star?? I'm not sure what one star Indian food would taste like, but this surely isn't it. I went on a Friday night and found most everything about Saffron to be first class. I arrived at Saffron expecting the place to be small, and indeed it is not large, but they have done a very nice job with the decor. One thing missing was some authentic Indian background music, but as it was the place was noisy enough that you probably couldn't have heard it anyway. C'est la vie. As others have noted, the food arrives piping hot from the kitchen. Portions could have been larger for some dishes - in retrospect I realize I received Vegetable Samosas instead of the Samosa Chaat that I ordered - $8 for 2 didn't make sense at the time. The Onion Bhajia was a typical Indian appetizer, though very tasty. For bread, the Garlic Naan we ordered was excellent, while the Peshawari Naan - with cashew, raisins and dried coconut - was a really nice compliment to the spiciness of the entrees. For our main dishes we both ordered lamb - the Boti Kabab Masala came in a small bowl and I initially thought it might not be enough food, but it turned out to be plenty. The presentation looked more like a soup, and there was plenty of sauce, but as it turned out plenty of meat as well. I am not sure how to describe the taste other than fairly traditional and not too spicy, a somewhat tomato based sauce - in any case I enjoyed it. The other main dish was Lamb with Turnip - a special that day - a more standard presentation with potatoes, lamb, and sauce - honestly this dish to me tasted not too much different than the other, so maybe we could have ordered more wisely for the sake of variety. For desert we had to have the traditional Ghulab Jamun - good, but more than two would have been nice - and Mango Kulfi ice cream, which was another special that evening. I was pleased by the the bright and modern decor, the attentiveness of the waiters to refill our water glasses, and the size of our bill - and I am glad I don't have to go downtown to have a decent Indian meal. (To be fair though, for the price, Tandoor India does give you somewhat larger portions, and I doubt I will stop being a fan of theirs any time soon.) I will definitely be returning to Saffron in the future. As Alton Brown would say, "good eats".

Ask for taste if you want to try something. Put as much or as little in the cup as you want. Stop by the dry topping section, then the chocolate/caramel station, then the fruit/other toppings. But then I put toppings on it - caramel (just a touch), chocolate, and some cookie dough chunks (real, moist, cookie dough!!!). The yogurt itself was yum and I loved it. I think though that I prefer little to no toppings on my ice cream/yogurt. I got sick of the cookie dough after just a couple of bites and then felt a little sick to my stomach (like too rich - and I almost NEVER say those words!!). SO that's my bad, not theirs. Next time I'm getting straight yogurt with perhaps some chocolate sauce on it and be done. The great thing is that you can do whatever you want. It is all YOU!

text: "Italian" food? HA! I don't think so. North is just another place trying to bank on the word 'Italian', without understanding what it means. North succeeds because it's a "shiny object" (on the outside, when you go inside you see filthy white chairs). Just because it seems fancy, doesn't mean it is. Let's start from the beginning. I was seated while my husband parked the car. A waiter came over and asked if I'd like water while I waited. Yes, please. Ten minutes after that, a different waiter greets us, and asks if we're ready to order food. Uh...can I have a drink first??? He apologizes, and takes our drink order. Another five to ten minutes later, and a THIRD waiter greets us. What the hell is going on? He seemed as confused as we were. We ask him for a few more minutes to look at the menu, and he seemed to get it together in that time. From then on, he was pretty good with the service. He even remembered when he brought us new bread that we didn't like the sun dried tomato butter, and brought us regular butter instead. Cool. On to the food. We started with the Zucca Chips. They describe them on the menu as "YUM!", which is the farthest from the truth as can be. These things were tasteless. No, let me correct myself. They tasted like oil. With some salt. They were soggy. They were not very good. My husband disagreed with me, but he likes fried foods far too much. I ordered the Bucatini for my entree. It was presented very sloppily. Worse, it was the most overcooked pasta I've had in a very long time. The sauce was watery, but it had ok flavor. The ricotta cheese on top was skimp. Actually, the entire dish was skimp. It was a very small portion for $14. And worse, there was some sort of herb that didn't get ground up well enough in my plate, and I chewed down on it, not thinking anything hard would be in my plate. It was like a pebble. That hurt my tooth, and I'm lucky it didn't do any damage. My husband ordered the hangar steak, which was cooked perfectly how he ordered it. The cheese on the top should have been a compound butter or something rather than just a small amount of crumbled cheese, though. Once the little bit of cheese was gone, he was only able to taste char. When the bites were good, though, he liked it very much. Nothing about this dish is Italian, though. The use of gorgonzola doesn't make it so. We sat for two hours in North, and I didn't even get to eat. The manager did comp my meal and offer me a new one, but we had to get home by that time. My tummy is still grumbling. Vero Amore makes better pasta (and probably pizza). The Abbey makes a MUCH BETTER version of the steak plate. I won't be back to the uninspired North any time soon.

text: Wow, where to begin... My friends and I got the Groupon for the Supper Show which supposedly included a four course tasting menu, four "premium" cocktails and the burlesque show which is usually about $50 per person but we got in for about half price, thank god. In all fairness the venue is fun, nicely decorated, etc. We were shown to our seats in a timely fashion (i'd made a reservation) where some plastic noisemakers and a giant ceramic plate of tasteless popcorn awaited. We joked that maybe this was the "first course." If only we'd known. Our waiter came by with a drink menu and after explaining to us that we could order four premium drinks as the Groupon indicated, he came back and told us he'd gotten it wrong, we could only order domestic drinks (beer, rum and coke, etc.) Okay, fine, no fancy drinkage. Not a huge deal. But then the real first course came... Bread and raisins. Oh and a few peanuts and assorted cheese slivers. Basically trail mix and a couple crackers. Hmm...not quite the gourmet appetizers you'd expect at $50 a plate. But we laughed it off and got ready to enjoy the show. The show wasn't half bad, but it wasn't half good either. Actually it was difficult to tell because the acts only lasted about 3 minutes before there was a 15 minute "break" so that we could be served our next delicious course. The MC was pretty corny (But i guess they're supposed to be) and the dancers were nothing special. The fire-eater was cool, but they brought him out twice...so it got old quick. Course two was a salad, which would have been fine with any semblance of dressing on it. Literally it was dry spinach leaves with a thin slice of smoked salmon on top. I thought maybe they just forgot mine, but no...none of us had any dressing of any kind, which pretty much made the salad inedible. The main course was actually decent, steak, potatoes, broccoli and texas toast. The desert was vanilla pudding being passed off as 'creme brulee' and a chocolate covered strawberry. We were already unimpressed when our check came. The drinks had been comped but there was a $32 dollar 'service fee' ($8 a piece) for...what? We didn't know. Apparently a service fee is pretty standard for these types of places but no where on the Groupon on anywhere else was it mentioned. When we asked the server he said it "should have been explained" to us either at the front door or in the Groupon. Well it wasn't. So from what we gathered, between dinner, drinks, tip and mysterious 'service fee,' without the Groupon we'd have been looking at about an $80-$100 night each. When we complained to the bartender she eventually let us leave without paying the service fee since it wasn't properly explained to us, which was something I guess. All in all, definitely will NOT be going back between the boring food, lackluster performance and hidden fees.

text: Possibly the worst real estate company out there. This is how the company works: You call and are assigned an office agent. The office agent is great, the so-called 'bait' for which you fall for. He is interested, knowledgeable, will match you with apartments that fit your needs. Then you go to see an apartment, and only one real estate agent out in the field is assigned to show that particular apartment so you have to work with them to schedule a viewing. If you like the apartment, you then pay an application fee (the most expensive in town, $50 per person) and are assured they will get back to you in 48 hours. WARNING: by applying, you also have to provide a one month deposit in the form of a certified check, and if you are approved and do not move in, for whatever reason, they reserve the right to keep your one month deposit. Once you are approved you will work once again with the listing agent (the one who showed you the place) to get your contract signed and voila, the apartment is yours. In essence, it sounds simple enough, but is, however, completely dependent on who your listing agent is. In our case, the company took 1 week to let us know if we were approved (from later conversations with the owner of the place, he wasn't even aware we existed until the lease was made), and then took 3 more weeks to produce a lease, that then took another week to alter with the things we had specifically requested when we applied for the apartment, which ultimately cost us a 'free month if lease signed by x' as we clearly signed three weeks after that due date. In the meantime, two other units had rented through another real estate company and the owner was just as flabbergasted as we were. Thank you, phillyaptco, for making what could have been a streamlined process, into an extremely harrowing, stressful, and painful process. I understand that it all depends on who your listing agent is, but that is exactly why this model doesn't work. You need to have one person in charge of everything for you, of selecting places, then showing them to you, then running your credit and then producing a lease, to have any sort of reasonable expectation that they will be held accountable for you. Veer away. In most cases the owners of a place will be working with more than one real estate company. Look up the address on the internet and go with more respectable companies that will be oh-so-much less painful.

text: I visited Mr An's for the teppanyaki and came away disappointed. My disappointment stems primarily from the disconnect between cost and quality. We spent $125 on dinner for three but the food was boring and, with one notable exception, just okay or even bad. The teppan show was certainly fun, but I felt like I was eating an $8 plate of food and spending $20 for the show. Our teppanyaki chef was most certainly a native but put on a ridiculously false Japanese accent for the duration of his time with us. He was fun, and entertaining, but seeing him perform the same four tricks and tell the same corny jokes as all of the other chefs made me wonder what is going on in the world of teppanyaki today. Are there no visionaries? If there are, they aren't at Mr An's. The teppan food was generally boring. The fried rice was peppered with vegetables that clearly came frozen in a bag and the fried noodles were soggy and flavored solely with soy sauce. The appetizer soup was basically reconstituted beef bouillon with some mushroom slices floating in it. The shrimp and scallops were horribly overcooked (tough shrimp and scallops are a sin). The steak, chicken, and veggies were fine, but when weighed against the rest the final result was a flop. The best thing about our visit was the calamari appetizer. The calamari was delicious and cooked to perfection, but the rest of the appetizer was disappointing. It was delicious calamari sitting on a bed of crunchy white noodles and practically raw white onion. Had the onion been cooked a bit longer this really could have been a standout dish. As it was, most of what came out on the plate went right back where it came from (without the delicious squid, of course). The sushi was uninspiring. The hamachi belly nagiri was okay, but the fish tasted like it was soon going to be too old to eat. It was also sliced very thinly, which is something I've never run into before and did not like. The spicy tuna roll was a big let down as well. Here's a staple sushi item that should be fantastic and it was just adequate. It is possible that my experience is not the norm. The place was busy when I arrived, so some people must like it enough to return. My recommendation is to give Mr An's a pass. I won't be returning. If I need entertainment with dinner I'll find it somewhere else.
label: NEG

text: I don't know why there wasn't already an added spot on Pennypack, but I'm creating one so now ppl can check in if they go for a walk in the woods on Pennypack Trail. There are no playgrounds, but it's great to have a near by place to de-stress and get back to nature for a little bit. Maybe even have a picnic! Watch out for worms, though. The woods are sadly overpopulated with a variety of worm species, which can be found simply by scraping back loose topsoil. It's a shame because they are destroying the soil and causing massive erosion. So if you need some bait for fishing, don't bother buying any, just walk along the trail and find hundreds. And especially don't dump any leftovers! They will procreate! RIP salamanders....you will be missed.

Just because the original installer couldn't fill out my warranty card properly with the correct roll #'s doesn't mean my tint is illegal. Even an untrained eye can see that my tint is not dark enough to be illegal. A window tint installer, obviously, should be able to see the difference. Even the customer waiting with me laughed when he overheard that my tint is "illegal". James was installing tint on this guy's truck that was a lot darker than my tint. So I left and took my car somewhere else so they could put a meter on it. The meter read 42% (40% or below is illegal in Louisiana). Unfortunately I have to deal with Shade Tree because they are the only ones in the area that install the window film that I use. Hopefully when I go back there this week James will have an approval from the warranty department to do the job. I am very very patient and can easily deal with rude or bad service but at least know your shit. If you only do one thing do it well if you want to have a thriving business.

text: If there were ratings for most odd experience in a restaurant, I'd give it 5 stars. But it gets 2 from me because service was marginal at best and downright poor at times. No problem. So I ask him what that might be tonight. He says he can't tell me. Despite numerous re-phrasings of my question, he insisted that there is no way to know what the chef will make. The chef will not tell me and the only input I may provide is if I have certain allergies. Then the chef will leave out those foods. But otherwise I cannot know before the dish arrives at the table. To make this my one and only time here, this place had the audacity to TURN OFF all the lights, and TV and give us the bill before we finished eating. Seriously, how do you want to treat your customers? I'm sure we are the reason your cash registers ring and repeat and loyal followers are established. I guess that is not in their business plan. Turning off the lights is very poor service. Prior to this incident, I would have been very positive on the food and only mentioned the dark lighting in passing, but the ending made eating here more of a waste of money. text: Absolutely amazing Spanish tapas. Came here on an impulse while actually on the way to another restaurant; pretty glad we stopped in after having five tapas that served as sort of pre-dinner appetizers. We arrived around opening time on the Tuesday after Hurricane Sandy hit Philadelphia, thus there was no wait time whatsoever. I'd imagine it to be a lot busier on most other nights. Service was exceptional; my friend was running out of charge on his phone and our waitress gladly found an outlet in the back for recharging. The restaurant was dimly lit and conveyed a classic yet cool vibe. And of course the food was spectacular. After starting off with a complimentary plate (I believe it was tuna served with thin tortillas), we received our tapas in order (the plates came quickly, but remember there were very few patrons in the restaurant at the time). The queso de cabra (goat cheese in a tomato basil sauce) was wonderful--the cheese was of perfect consistency, although more bread could have been provided initially. We also got the Spanish tortillas and chiperones fritas (fried baby squid), both of which were great. However, the knockout punch had to be the datiles con almendras--an almond set within dates wrapped in bacon, placed on a skewer with onions. The texture was perfect, the sweet/salty flavor simply amazing, and I just could not stop thinking about the dish long after I finished. Wow. Pros: Freakin' delicious tapas Cons: Too far from where I live; return date as yet unknown

text: I'm surprised it took me so long to make it to Zahav but I FINALLY MADE IT on Friday for Restaurant Week. My she-date (aka, Stephen S.'s Yelpless fiance) who usually eats meat accompanied me on a vegetarian journey through their RW menu. We started off with the two must-trys: the salatim and hummus with laffa. The salatim was impressive - although the eight portions of various salads are small, it was a pretty filling appetizer. I sampled everything and enjoyed the wide array of flavors and textures. The dates were the bomb and the tabbouleh was some of the best. Why is it when I try to cook with parsley it tastes like ass but they make a light, seemingly simple tabbouleh and it tastes like a totally different leaf? WTFFF my life. But this is probably because I do not cook at Zahav. Anyways, it was good. The laffa was served steaming hot and the hummous was tasty but did not revolutionize the way I see hummous. Next time, I'll go for the highly-recommended Turkish hummous blend. In short, here's what we wound up with for the remainder of our meal: haloumi, fried cauliflower, artichoke halves, smoked salmon, pumpkin, eggplant, almond semifreddo and poached pineapple. All were delicious, the fried cauliflower being the obvious stand out among the smallest plates. The eggplant tasted unlike any eggplant either of us had ever had. It was rich and buttery, which wwas balanced nicely by the barley beneath. The almond semifreddo, topped with a crispy, snappy disc of chocolate was my dessert of choice. By the time dessert arrived, I was relieved as I filled up QUICK. I'd love to come back and try their a la carte menu as soon as possible but I still think I got a fairly complete scope of what they have to offer via their RW menu. The service was basic and a little hurried, as it usually is during RW, but the attention paid by those attending to our table other than our hustling server was great. The general ambiance and atmosphere of the restaurant is busy and bustling without being blinding and loud. I love it here, can't wait to return.

text: I've been a frequentor of AC for years, and have always bit my tongue when it came to the consistently grotesque service offered up by front of house, wait staff, bus staff, etc. The food is on the higher end of mediocre (their mussels in red range from "a little fishy" to "finding Nemo", so you just have to catch them on a better night), the location is convenient, and the prices are light on the wallet. Much to our expectation, the front of house greeted us with a gust of rudeness "BACK UP!" he exclaimed to our party of 6. "I DIDN'T CALL YOU YET!!!!". Whoa. But, back up, we did, because we were pretty certain the table of old folks eyin' up their check and gathering their to-go containers were our key to tasteless flatbread and hummus in need of just a BIT more salt. In time, the folks got up, but to our dismay, like a gust of wind, a DIFFERENT part of 6 swept in the door and filed into the table! Immediately, a few friends rushed the "host", because at this point the wait time had far extended our original estimate of 1.75 hours (cue "bullshit cough"). Smugly, he offered us a table for 4, and we're all friends (and hungry friends, at that), so we complied. Now, please know that admittedly I have a bit of a temper. Up until this point I had kept my cool purely because I'm well aware that AC is a complete joke of a business, and I was voluntarily putting myself through the horror that they call restaurant service. So, we pile into the 4-top, and I can't help but notice the bus-boy, YES BUS-BOY, looking a little red in the face and mumbling under his breath. Then, it happened, "YOU'RE ALL GONNA NEED TO BACK UP", he yelped (ha, ironic). One "back up" command is sickening, but two will send me flying off the handle: "YOU'RE ALL gonna need to be more polite! And learn how to run a business!", I retaliated. And then, with the most spectacular condescending tone that could exit from a struggggggling hipster's mouth, "OH YEAH?? DO WE?? DO WE?? I DON'T GIVE A SHIT". With that, I grabbed my friends and my wine and exited the premises, never to return again. On the up side, we headed down to Han Dynasty, where Han, himself, greeted us with a lovely table for 6 accompanied by a lazy susan of delicious chinese cuisine, and the following message to our Yelp community, "I won't curse at you, I'll curse with you."

text: Five years ago, this place would have received a glowing five star review from me. I ate here the first time I ever came to New Orleans. I eventually moved to New Orleans and this used to be one of my favorite places to eat AND favorite places to bring out of town guests. There menu used to be a lot larger, they had amazing specials and the food was a lot more like fine dining. I loved it as a local and I loved it when I was a tourist. Sadly I had to leave New Orleans and no longer live there. BUT I do get back every year or two to visit friends. Naturally I always want to go back to this place since it was a favorite. Unfortunately over the last three years or so something has happened. The menu got more and more limited, service went downhill, and the food majorly took a dive. The final straw for this place was my visit two weeks ago. I was so excited to take my boyfriend to all the amazing places in New Orleans (especially places to eat). We were seated and served water right away. The server took our drink order and disappeared. After twenty minutes we started to stand up to leave and she suddenly came back. text: I finally made my way into the dark and popular Bern's Steakhouse. I was excited because I heard how well-known its aged steaks in town. The attire is supposed to be dressy, but I dressed it somewhat dressy casual blouse and jeans. The atmosphere is definitely romantic, but I saw couples and even parties of 4 or more. So it seemed pretty nice and comfortable. Our table was in the corner with a little bit of privacy. I liked the decor. Although, when trying to find the nearest restroom, it was like walking into a maze. The menu is very extensive. It literally is a book, but it has mostly the descriptions of the different types of steaks that they offer in different cuts and sizes. Everything is broken down for you. But it was a bit overwhelming. My friend was able to help me narrow it down and ordered our 20oz. Chateaubriand steak with ease. My eyes widen when I heard that. Apparently, we were to split that fortunately. We also started our meal with a bottle of American champagne, paired with cheese crackers. They were actually pretty good. The steak comes with fixed appetizers such a french-onion soup and mixed micro salad with my choice of vinaigrette dressing. Both were really good. We also got our own plates with our steak that came with multiple sides: baked potato, fried onions, and a bit of veggies. The steak was enormous and flavorful. I can taste hints of the garlic, which I love. But I did try to opt for a wine sauce to add more flavor. I thought the steak was tender and juicy, but I think I liked it better paired with a sauce to cut the saltiness. The service was spot on. Our server was nice and patient, and got what we needed right away gracefully. I thought it was a nice night for a Wednesday night, the place was almost full. After paying the bill, we decided to go through the tour inside the kitchen. (With wine, my friend's 2 dry martinis and our steak dinners, cost about $180 including gratuity already added). The dessert room is also like a dark maze. Each room is secluded and has its own phone booth where you can change music to your taste from classical to jazz. The menu is also extensive because it also includes the port wines that can be paired with the desserts. Instead of just glancing at the menu too long, we asked our waiter for the top 3 most popular desserts or his favorites. He gave us a cute story behind the ever popular Macadamia ice cream, which took Bern's 7 years to perfect. So needless to say, we opted for that one. Might I say, the 3 scoops were enormous and on top of that came with whole macadamias, a waffle bowl and chocolate sauce. It was rich and delightful. I would go back just for the dessert ($11). It was a real treat. But the reason for the 4 starts was the pricing. It's very pricey and a place that I would never frequent unless I had a major account. So for those that would like to try this ever popular steakhouse, try the steaks and go for the dessert. But be sure your wallet can afford to fork over that $$$ price tag, or someone else'.

text: I'm an idiot... I ordered a salad at a burger bar... The ambiance of the place reminds me of a prison. Concrete floors and walls. Exposed steel conduit for wiring. The light fixtures even had metal cages around them. All those hard surfaces reflected the sound too... and entering the place you're swallowed into the noise. The wait for two this Saturday was not long... about 30 minutes. There is open seating at a long bar, but we opted to wait for a table upstairs. Upstairs 'loft' seating must be the best use of these downtown building spaces... Bridge Tap has the same concept. But neither has figured out how to make it comfortable near the ceiling. The air is hot and stuffy considering you're sitting above a kitchen and about 75 other people. On to the food. For starters we had the pretzel sticks and wings. The place prides itself on making many of their ingredients (bread, ketchup, ice cream, etc.) in house. The cheese sauce with the pretzel sticks was an example. At first glance the bowl of queso looks like your typical processed nacho cheese. However, upon tasting it was clear that this is credible cheese melted down. Super yummy. I didn't care for the wings that much. They were apple tasting (it said this on the menu too)... and they were small. For entrees, I ordered a St. Louis salad and added bacon to it. It was HUGE. I doubt anyone could ever finish one of these. It was ok. The size gives it value, and I enjoyed the bits of summer cooked sausage cut up in it. However, the red onions and olives were way too bitter. She ordered a burger... but for whatever reason wanted to try the Vegan bun. She's not vegan. And food made for vegans may suit their diets, but this thing was awful. It came out like cornbread without flavor. Just falling apart and helplessly trying to hold together a burger and toppings. Upon realizing the ordering mistake, she ate the burger with a fork. The side of fried green tomatoes were perfect. The sauces for the fries and sides were home made and great. All in all, I was a bit underwhelmed. This is partly my own fault for ordering the stuff I did... but at 10 bucks a burger, the shiznit better be over the top... and it wasn't. Even at two stars, I'm pretty sure we'll go back, and stick to more traditional options.

text: Atchafalaya was a very pleasant surprise. We started with the fried green tomatoes topped with the sweetest lump blue crab and the crab free form ravioli with shiitake beurre blanc. I could have happily reordered both, but we moved on to shrimp and grits and boudin stuffed quail. The head on shrimp were cooked to succulent perfection and the grits were rich with butter and cheese, absolutely the best I have had. The quail was beautifully presented on tangy collard greens and puréed sweet potatoes and was delicious as well. The service was friendly and attentive and the owner was gracious as well as passionate about the hospitality industry. We lingered over coffee and an excellent red velvet cake while they called a cab for us and were never rushed. Much to my chagrin when we went downstairs to wait for the delayed cab, there was a crowd of people waiting. I hope everyone who waited had just as enjoyable a meal as we did and we apologize for keeping the table an extra ten minutes, definitely 5 stars!
